jobs.title: Policy Governance Professional
jobs.excerpt: Become a part of our caring community The Policy Governance Professional supports the Medicaid Utilization Management Policy Governance program.
jobs.description:
Become a part of our caring community

The Policy Governance Professional supports the Medicaid Utilization Management Policy Governance program. Reporting to the Policy Governance Lead, the primary responsibility of this role is to manage the end-to-end Medicaid UM Rates and Timeliness evaluation and reporting process across applicable markets, including physical health and behavioral health. Responsibilities include coordinating reporting schedules and data validation with accountable teams, evaluating performance trends, investigating potential contributing factors with operational and clinical stakeholders, developing clear written evaluations and recommendations, coordinating physician leadership review and committee approval, and tracking follow-up actions and supporting documentation. The role supports coordination of other UM-related QIE elements as responsibilities are established.

Job Responsibilities

o Own and coordinate the end-to-end NCQA UM Rates and Timeliness Report process across applicable Medicaid markets and lines of business.

o Manage reporting calendars, milestones, stakeholder responsibilities, data collection, validation, approvals, and final deliverables.

o Partner with operational, analytical, clinical, quality, compliance, accreditation, and market teams to resolve data issues and report risks.

o Analyze results to identify trends, outliers, performance concerns, and opportunities for improvement.

o Coordinate, document, and monitor corrective or follow-up actions, escalating overdue or high-risk items as appropriate.

o Prepare reporting summaries and materials for review by Utilization Management Committees, leadership, and other governance bodies.

o Maintain complete, organized, and audit-ready documentation supporting reporting results, decisions, approvals, and committee oversight.

o Support broader Policy Governance activities, including committee operations, policy lifecycle processes, regulatory alignment, process documentation, and continuous improvement.

o The role also supports related policy governance, accreditation, compliance, and process-improvement activities.


Use your skills to make an impact

Required Qualifications

o Bachelor’s degree

o Experience in healthcare industry (operations, utilization management, quality, compliance, accreditation, reporting, governance, or a related area.)

o Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, SharePoint, and related collaboration or tracking tools.

Preferred Qualifications

o Experience supporting Medicaid managed care or another government-sponsored healthcare program.

o Knowledge of NCQA accreditation standards and experience supporting accreditation survey preparation.

o Experience supporting governance committees or other formal oversight bodies.

o Experience interpreting regulatory, contractual, accreditation, or policy requirements.

o Experience coordinating corrective actions, performance improvement activities, or audit responses.

o Familiarity with data validation, reporting controls, and centralized national/state policy governance models.

jobs.description:
As Lead of Sales Strategy & Operations for Global Specialist and RX Sales, you will be the strategic thought partner to the Chief Business Officer and Global Head of Strategic Sales. You will own the analytics, plans, and plays that drive the RX and specialist organization, and you will turn data into clear GTM recommendations and run the operating rhythm that executes them.

The RX team brings our latest products to market. They work on taking our products from 0-1 in Sales and build the Sales plays that get handed over to the Core Sales team. Specialty Sales is tasked with increasing our product penetration for prospects and customers.

You will sit between the RX and specialist sales team and the broader Sales, Sales Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Customer Success organizations. Your job is to be the strategic thought partner to Global heads of Sales for RX and Specialist Sales; help them see around the corners and flag what to focus on and build the right GTM plays and execute.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Strategic Partnership: Act as the right hand to the Chief Business Officer and Global Head of Specialty Sales. Own the specialist team’s annual and quarterly plans, priorities, and executive narrative.
  • GTM Play Recommendations: Analyze pipeline, win/loss, attach, and whitespace data to identify where specialists create the most impact. Recommend, design, and track plays, then measure their results.
  • Reporting & Analytics: Build and maintain dashboards and models covering coverage, conversion, productivity, and attainment. Be the source of truth for team performance.
  • Coverage, Quota & Territory Design: Partner with Sales Leadership and Finance to define specialist coverage models, quota and capacity plans, territory alignment, and the rules for engaging with core sales teams.
  • Operating Cadence & Forecasting: Run the analytical deliverables for QBRs, forecast reviews, and annual planning. Surface risks and opportunities early.
  • Executive Communication: Present data-backed recommendations to the Leadership team, GTM executives, and cross-functional heads. Influence priorities and contribute to board-level deliverables.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Work with Marketing, Product, and Finance to align on shared metrics and tracking performance.
  • Team Leadership: Lead, mentor, and develop individuals on the team. Set standards for analytical rigor and business communication.

Experience You’ll Need:

  • 6+ years in GTM strategy, sales operations, revenue operations, business operations, or management consulting at a high-growth B2B SaaS or enterprise technology company.
  • Leadership: Direct people management experience, or a proven record of leading cross-functional initiatives in a matrixed environment.
  • Technical proficiency:
    • Understanding of Salesforce data architecture, opportunity lifecycle, and pipeline objects.
    • Advanced Excel or financial modeling for capacity planning, ramp, and ROI analysis.
  • Business acumen: Strong command of enterprise SaaS metrics and motions.
  • Executive presence: Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can turn complex data into a concise recommendation for C-level audiences and present it.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Computer Science, Statistics, Economics, or a related quantitative field. MBA or Master’s is a plus.

jobs.title: General Manager, Line of Credit
jobs.excerpt: Founded in 2017, NinjaHoldings works to give everyday Americans better access to financial services than traditional institutions typically provide.
jobs.description:
Founded in 2017, NinjaHoldings works to give everyday Americans better access to financial services than traditional institutions typically provide. Through our CreditNinja and NinjaCard brands, we offer digital banking and lending products designed for consumers often overlooked, paired with incentives that support long-term financial improvement. Our Edge brand extends this expertise to other companies, providing underwriting, fraud detection, and analytics services. Headquartered in Chicago with a distributed global workforce, we are a lean, growing organization committed to advancing consumer finance in the US.

Job Summary

CreditNinja is seeking an entrepreneurial General Manager to own and scale its line of credit (LOC) business. The LOC is a revolving credit product: customers draw on a credit limit, repay, and draw again. The General Manager will sharpen its economics, grow its customer base, and turn an early-stage product into a durable, profitable business line. Reporting to the President of CreditNinja Lending, the General Manager will hold full P&L responsibility. This covers strategy, product, growth, credit, capital, operations, and financial performance. The ideal candidate is a hands-on operator who has taken a revolving credit or consumer lending business from early traction to meaningful scale. This is a fully remote, U.S.-based position.

Key Responsibilities:

  • P&L Ownership: Own the full P&L for the LOC business line. Drive revenue and profitability targets while managing risk-adjusted returns, and take the business from early traction to meaningful scale
  • Strategy & Scale: Refine and execute the strategy to grow the LOC into a durable, differentiated product. Define how the LOC works alongside our installment loans so that together they serve more customers
  • Economics & Line Management: Sharpen unit economics across the account life cycle: opening credit limits, line increases, draws, utilization, pricing, and repayment. Build strong, repeatable returns at scale
  • Growth & Customer Acquisition: Work with Marketing to grow new accounts across direct, partner, and mobile app channels. Increase repeat use and lifetime customer value, and own the growth plan for the business
  • Product & Technology: Work with product and engineering to improve the digital customer experience, from application to draws, payments, and account management. Drive acquisition, engagement, and retention
  • Credit & Risk: Work with Credit, Risk, and Analytics to optimize underwriting, credit line strategy, pricing, and portfolio monitoring. Balance growth with sound credit outcomes
  • Capital & Funding: Build and scale the funding strategy in coordination with Finance and Capital Markets. Support growth in balances and optimize the cost of capital
  • Team Building: Build out and develop a high-performing, cross-functional team as the business scales, fostering a culture of ownership, accountability, and speed
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Coordinate across Marketing, Operations, Finance, Legal, Compliance, and Technology to align the LOC business with broader company objectives

Ideal Candidate Will Have:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in consumer lending, fintech, or financial services, including senior leadership roles with direct P&L ownership
  • Demonstrated success scaling an early-stage business line or product into a profitable operation, ideally in lines of credit, credit cards, or other revolving credit
  • Strong command of revolving credit economics: credit line assignment and management, utilization, pricing, credit and portfolio performance, and the drivers of a profitable lending P&L
  • Proven ability to grow a digital consumer credit product through marketing channels, partnerships, and customer engagement
  • Working knowledge of the regulatory environment for consumer lending, including open-end credit (TILA and Regulation Z, ECOA, FCRA, UDAAP, and related state and federal requirements)
  • Experience serving subprime or near-prime consumers preferred
  • Entrepreneurial, hands-on operator who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is comfortable with change and ambiguity
  • Exceptional leadership, communication, and analytical skills, with the ability to influence across all levels of an organization
  • Ability and drive to take ownership of the business and its outcomes

Benefits & Perks:

  • Flexible Paid Time Off
  • Health Benefits with generous medical, dental and vision insurance plans
  • 401(k) with matching contribution
  • Paid Family Leave
  • Annual Wellness & WFH Subsidies
  • Employee Referral Program
  • Remote first culture with convenient downtown office in the heart of the city

jobs.description:
Transmission Engineering Lead (PE)

Position Description

Vantage Point Solutions (VPS) is seeking a Transmission Engineering Lead to provide technical leadership, project oversight, and client engagement for electric utility transmission projects. In this role, you will work directly with utility clients to plan, analyze, design, and oversee construction of transmission solutions that align with client goals and support reliable electric service.

Projects may include new transmission, demolitions, rebuilds, reconductors, and system improvement initiatives. You will serve as a key link between utility personnel, contractors, field crews, and engineering teams, helping to move projects from concept through commissioning. Types of transmission lines may include tower, pole, and underground transmission lines and equipment.

The Transmission Engineering Lead is responsible for the technical direction, design oversight, and professional engineering approval of transmission projects. The role provides mentorship and leadership to engineers, maintains client relationships, and ensures projects are completed safely, with quality, on schedule, and within budget.

Successful candidates demonstrate strong leadership, sound engineering judgment, adaptability, attention to detail, and a commitment to delivering exceptional service.

Why Vantage Point Solutions?

Vantage Point Solutions was founded in 2002 on the belief that people come first. Today, VPS is a customer focused, technology-driven engineering and consulting firm serving clients in the power, broadband, and financial industries.

We are committed to delivering exceptional service while fostering a culture built on teamwork, accountability, respect, innovation, and professional growth. Our employees are empowered to make meaningful contributions to our clients, communities, and industries while building rewarding careers.

Technical Leadership & Project Management:

  • Lead and manage multiple transmission projects simultaneously from planning through construction and commissioning.
  • Conduct quality assurance and quality control reviews throughout all phases of project delivery.
  • Ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in compliance with local, state, and federal technical, regulatory, and safety standards.
  • Conduct quality assurance and quality control reviews throughout all phases of project delivery.
  • Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, and engineering cost estimates.
  • Stay current with applicable codes, standards, industry practices, and emerging technologies.

Engineering & Design

  • Perform system-wide planning studies and system assessments related to transmission capacity, reliability, and system performance, applying best practices and the latest technologies.
  • Develop, review, and approve (PE-seal) complete transmission designs, including equipment and material ratings, plan and profile drawings, sag and tension tables, structure drawings, staking sheets, and bills of material to deliver construction drawings (IFC) and bid packages (IFB).
  • Prepare equipment specifications, material specifications, and construction requirements in accordance with client and regulatory requirements.
  • Professionally seal for-construction transmission designs.
  • Demonstrate proficiency with industry-standard software used for the design, planning, modeling, and analysis of transmission, protection systems, and control systems.
  • Support permitting, regulatory compliance, and engineering documentation efforts.
  • Support Geotech, structural, and civil engineering in relation to transmission lines.

Client & Field Support

  • Establish and maintain effective working relationships with clients, contractors, utility personnel, and internal team members.
  • Strengthens VPS’s reputation as a trusted partner for utilities and enterprise clients.
  • Serve as a trusted technical advisor to utility clients and assist in developing best practices, infrastructure modernization, and operational direction.
  • Provide field engineering support during construction, commissioning, outage restoration, and emergency response activities.
  • Assist clients with day-to-day engineering questions, operational challenges, and strategic planning initiatives.
  • Assist clients in meeting regulatory reporting and compliance requirements for transmission and distribution systems.

Team Leadership

  • Mentor, train, and develop engineers and technical staff. Develop a high-performing engineering team capable of executing complex, multi-faceted projects.
  • Foster collaboration, accountability, and technical excellence within the Power Engineering team.
  • Support management and customer relations staff with business development initiatives.
  • Support recruiting, onboarding, and professional development efforts.
  • Implement process improvements to enhance engineering efficiency, accuracy, and client satisfaction.

Required Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Civil Engineering (BSEE) or Electrical Engineering Technology (BSEET) from an ABET-accredited institution, preferably with an emphasis in Power Systems.
  • Active Professional Engineer (PE) license and ability to obtain licensure in other states through reciprocity within a reasonable timeframe.
  • Minimum of 10 years of experience in electric utility transmission design and engineering.
  • Minimum of 2 years of engineering leadership experience with direct supervisory responsibilities.
  • Demonstrated success working with utility personnel, construction contractors, and multidisciplinary project teams.
  • Strong knowledge of tower, pole, and underground transmission design, system analysis, structure support, transmission protection and controls, and utility construction practices.
  • Thorough understanding of applicable engineering standards and codes, including NESC, IEEE, ANSI, and RUS requirements.
  • Working knowledge of OSHA requirements applicable to transmission and the electric utility industry.
  • Broad understanding of electric utility operations, including transmission, substations, distribution systems, protection and control systems, SCADA, AMI, and OMS platforms.
  • Ability and willingness to perform field work, including walking on uneven or rough terrain, visiting active construction sites, and working in varying weather conditions.

Additional Qualifications & Requirements:

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with clients, contractors, utility personnel, regulatory agencies, and internal team members.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, sound engineering judgment, and attention to detail.
  • Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
  • Authorized to work in the United States.
  • Ability to successfully pass background checks, driving record reviews, drug screening requirements, and client-specific screening processes as required.

Compensation and Benefits:

VPS offers a competitive compensation package along with comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, a 401(k)-retirement plan, paid time off, professional development opportunities, and other benefits designed to support the well-being and success of our employees.


Equal Employment Opportunity

Vantage Point Solutions is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.”

About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

  • Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

  • People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

  • Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical / engineering leadership interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

As a global leader, Pavion specializes in the design, installation, service, and maintenance of cutting-edge fire alarm systems, critical communications, video surveillance, access control, and advanced AV technologies. With a commitment to safety, reliability, and operational excellence, Pavion ensures scalable, future-ready solutions tailored to meet and exceed our clients’ needs. Learn more at .

Pavion is seeking an experienced and strategic Director of Environmental, Health & Safety (EH&S) to lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the company's environmental, health, and safety programs across its operations.

This individual will establish a consistent, proactive safety culture throughout the organization, supporting field technicians, installation teams, project managers, service personnel, warehouse operations, and corporate employees. The Director will partner with executive leadership, regional and business unit leaders, Human Resources, Operations, and project teams to identify and mitigate risks, ensure compliance with applicable regulations, and drive measurable improvements in workplace safety.

The ideal candidate combines strategic leadership with hands-on operational experience in construction, electrical contracting, fire and life-safety systems, security integration, or a related technical services environment. This leader will be responsible for developing scalable safety programs that support Pavion's continued growth while ensuring employees and subcontractors have the training, tools, and resources necessary to work safely.

Primary Responsibilities:

EH&S Strategy and Leadership

  • Develop and execute a comprehensive, company-wide EH&S strategy aligned with Pavion's business objectives, operational requirements, and commitment to employee safety.
  • Establish standardized safety policies, procedures, programs, and performance expectations across business units and geographic regions.
  • Build and promote a proactive safety culture that emphasizes accountability, employee engagement, hazard recognition, and continuous improvement.
  • Partner with executive leadership and operational leaders to integrate safety into business planning, project execution, and day-to-day operations.
  • Establish measurable EH&S objectives, key performance indicators (KPIs), and reporting processes to monitor performance and drive accountability.
  • Provide regular updates to executive leadership regarding safety performance, emerging risks, regulatory developments, and improvement initiatives.

Regulatory Compliance and Risk Management

  • Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local environmental, health, and safety regulations, including OSHA and EPA requirements.
  • Maintain and continuously improve EH&S policies and programs applicable to field service, construction, installation, maintenance, warehouse, and office environments.
  • Conduct risk assessments, job hazard analyses, site safety reviews, and operational audits to identify potential hazards and implement corrective actions.
  • Oversee the development and maintenance of required safety documentation, records, permits, and compliance reporting.
  • Monitor regulatory changes and communicate their potential impact to the organization.
  • Support regulatory inspections, investigations, and interactions with applicable government agencies.
  • Evaluate insurance, workers' compensation, and operational loss trends to identify opportunities for risk reduction in partnership with the appropriate internal stakeholders.

Field and Project Safety

  • Establish safety standards for technicians, installers, project managers, service personnel, and subcontractors working at customer locations and construction sites.
  • Ensure appropriate programs are in place for electrical safety, fall protection, ladder and lift safety, lockout/tagout, personal protective equipment (PPE), hazard communication, and other relevant workplace hazards.
  • Partner with Operations and Project Management to incorporate safety planning into project mobilization, customer-site requirements, and field execution.
  • Develop processes to assess customer-site conditions, identify hazards, and establish appropriate controls before work begins.
  • Establish and oversee subcontractor safety qualification, onboarding, training, and performance-monitoring requirements.
  • Promote consistent adherence to customer-specific safety requirements and applicable site access and work authorization procedures.
  • Conduct periodic field visits and site inspections to verify compliance and reinforce safe work practices.

Training and Safety Culture

  • Develop and oversee company-wide EH&S training programs tailored to employees' roles, responsibilities, and exposure to workplace hazards.
  • Ensure employees receive required safety orientations, refresher training, and task-specific instruction.
  • Equip managers and supervisors with the knowledge and resources necessary to lead safety discussions, conduct job hazard assessments, and address unsafe conditions.
  • Promote employee participation in safety meetings, toolbox talks, hazard reporting, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Establish effective communication channels for sharing safety alerts, lessons learned, and best practices across the organization.
  • Evaluate training effectiveness and maintain appropriate training records and certifications.

Incident Management and Continuous Improvement

  • Lead or oversee the investigation of workplace injuries, near misses, property damage, environmental incidents, and other safety-related events.
  • Identify root causes and implement corrective and preventive actions to reduce the likelihood of recurrence.
  • Track incident trends, recordable injuries, lost-time incidents, near misses, and corrective action completion.
  • Partner with Human Resources, Operations, and other stakeholders on workers' compensation cases, return-to-work coordination, and appropriate workplace accommodations.
  • Develop and implement initiatives to reduce injury frequency, severity, lost workdays, and associated costs.
  • Ensure timely and accurate incident reporting in accordance with applicable legal and company requirements.

Environmental Management

  • Oversee environmental compliance programs applicable to Pavion's operations, including hazardous materials management, waste disposal, spill prevention, and other relevant environmental requirements.
  • Establish procedures for the appropriate handling, storage, transportation, and disposal of regulated materials where applicable.
  • Assess environmental risks associated with field operations, facilities, equipment, and project activities.
  • Maintain required environmental documentation and coordinate inspections, reporting, and corrective actions as needed.
  • Promote responsible environmental practices and continuous improvement in environmental performance.

Business Integration and Organizational Growth

  • Collaborate with Operations, Human Resources, Legal, Fleet, and business unit leadership to align safety practices with broader business processes.
  • Support the integration of acquired businesses by assessing existing safety programs, identifying gaps, and implementing consistent company standards.
  • Develop scalable policies, training resources, and reporting tools that support a growing, geographically dispersed organization.
  • Evaluate EH&S systems, technology, and processes to improve visibility, standardization, and operational efficiency.
  • Build relationships with customers, subcontractors, insurance partners, and external safety professionals to strengthen the company's overall risk management approach.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental Health, Industrial Safety, Environmental Science, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in environmental health and safety, occupational safety, or risk management, including leadership responsibility.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and implementing EH&S programs across multiple locations, business units, or field-based operations.
  • Strong working knowledge of OSHA regulations and applicable environmental compliance requirements.
  • Experience supporting construction, electrical contracting, industrial services, fire protection, security integration, facilities services, or a related technical field environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to conduct risk assessments, safety audits, incident investigations, root-cause analyses, and corrective action planning.
  • Experience developing safety training programs and influencing safe work practices among field employees, managers, and subcontractors.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to influence stakeholders at all organizational levels and drive accountability without relying solely on formal authority.
  • Willingness to travel to field locations, customer sites, and company facilities as business needs require.
  • International Safety Regulations a plus

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental Health, or a related discipline.
  • Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH), or another relevant professional certification.
  • Experience managing EH&S programs in a multi-state, multi-site organization.
  • Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, and integration of safety programs across diverse operating businesses.
  • Familiarity with workers' compensation trends, insurance loss control, fleet safety, and safety performance analytics.
  • Experience implementing EH&S management systems, digital safety platforms, and company-wide compliance reporting.
  • Knowledge of NFPA standards and electrical safety standards relevant to fire protection, life-safety systems, and electrical installation work.

jobs.description:
Data Scientist - iwocaPay Credit Risk Modelling

Hybrid in London, United Kingdom (one day per week in office requirement)

We're looking for a Data Scientist to join the iwocaPay Risk Squad.

You'll own credit models that decide who iwocaPay can safely fund, on what terms, and how far the product can grow. You'll help shape how risk modelling develops.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don't wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that's as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We've already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Risk Squad owns credit risk and fraud for iwocaPay, iwoca's Buy Now Pay Later product for businesses. The aim is to lend to every business likely to repay, and to spot the ones that aren't.

The squad works across three areas:

  • Lending decisions. Building and improving the automated credit model.

  • The portfolio. Tracking losses, chargebacks, and seller performance, and deciding which segments to grow or pull back from.

  • New products. Designing the risk side of each one before it launches.

The squad is small and new – two data scientists, a risk analyst and a risk lead.

The role

As a Data Scientist in the Risk Squad, you'll co-own every credit model with the other data scientist and review one another's work. The job is mostly supervised ML on tabular data, with a fair amount of data engineering as the squad moves onto its own pipelines. You'll start on the automated credit model and take on the invoice financing models over time. You can also test ideas with iwoca's other lending data science teams, who work on similar credit problems.

You'll choose what to work on and write the plans you deliver. Much of the squad's work happens in iwocaPay's product and strategy meetings, so your models shape the roadmap. You'll also help set up how the squad works – what it monitors, and the guidelines it follows.

Live project examples:

  • Model architecture. Rethinking the model around how iwocaPay actually lends: overlapping facilities, short terms, and a growing set of products a customer can use.

  • Blending datasets. Bringing more iwocaPay-specific data into the models while still drawing on iwoca's larger core lending dataset, through methods such as transfer learning.

  • Invoice financing. Building a credit risk model from scratch for a new product on a segment iwoca hasn’t lent to before. Plus finding the modelling opportunities elsewhere in the funnel, like in our offers...

The requirements

Essential:

  • Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field – typically a degree or Master's in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, or similar. You reason about uncertainty and calibration as first-order concerns.

  • Production ML. You have built supervised ML models on tabular data end to end – exploration, training, deployment, and monitoring.

  • Ownership. You work well in a small, early-stage team where priorities move quickly. You build what you need as you go, and take loosely defined problems from framing to a landed decision.

  • Judgement. You know when a model is good enough to go live, and when it needs more work. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right.

  • AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – a modelling pipeline, a prototype, or a tool others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail for non-technical colleagues in product, risk, and leadership.

Bonus:

  • Domain experience. You have worked in credit risk modelling or lending.

  • Non-linear methods. You have used gradient boosting or neural networks on tabular data in production.

  • Combining datasets. You have used transfer learning, domain adaptation, or similar methods on data sources of different size and relevance.

  • Data engineering. You have built data pipelines and managed datasets alongside your modelling work.

  • Coding. You can write code for analysis. The squad works in Python.

The salary

We expect to pay from £60,000 to £80,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Compensation Range: £60K - £90K

About Crunchbase

Crunchbase is a predictive solution that provides intelligence on private companies, powered by the unique combination of live private company data, AI, and market activity from over 80 million users. We predict private market movements that matter to help investors, dealmakers, and analysts make the right decisions.

We are committed to fostering a positive, diverse, and inclusive culture by hiring for potential and embracing individuals with diverse perspectives, backgrounds, experiences, and skill sets. We value transparency and openness, believing that an inclusive environment strengthens our teams and enhances our products.

About the Role

The Senior Product Manager, AI & Data Science Products owns Crunchbase’s customer-facing AI data layer: proprietary data and intelligence generated from foundational data using AI and machine learning.

The primary charter is to identify high-value opportunities for new model-derived data, validate their value with customers, and take successful products from experimentation through scaled adoption.

Success is measured by three outcomes:

  • New differentiated data: Create proprietary intelligence that Crunchbase could not practically produce through collection alone.
  • Higher customer value: Help customers discover, understand, evaluate, and prioritize their private market jobs more effectively.
  • Revenue and adoption: Turn valuable AI data into measurable usage, retention, expansion, and monetization opportunities.

What You’ll Do

AI & Data Science Product Strategy

  • Own the strategy and roadmap for Crunchbase’s customer-facing AI data layer.
  • Identify high-value opportunities for new predictions, classifications, signals, and insights that improve customer decisions.
  • Build a differentiated portfolio of AI data products rather than isolated AI features.
  • Partner with Foundational Data to determine when customer needs are best addressed through collected, acquired, inferred, predicted, or generated data.

Customer Discovery & Product Development

  • Work directly with customers to identify where new or better data can materially improve their workflows and decisions.
  • Rapidly test new AI data concepts, validate customer value, and scale successful products.
  • Define how model-derived data, including confidence and uncertainty, should be presented to customers.
  • Partner with Design, Engineering, and Data Science to deliver AI data across Crunchbase products, APIs, MCP, and data delivery experiences.

Quality & Product Economics

  • Balance customer value, coverage, accuracy, freshness, and generation cost.
  • Monitor product and data performance and continuously improve quality based on customer feedback and observed outcomes.

Adoption & Monetization

  • Partner with Go-to-Market on positioning, customer education, and launch strategy.
  • Partner with Pricing and Packaging and Sales to identify monetization opportunities.
  • Measure adoption, retention, expansion, revenue, and customer outcomes to determine which products to scale, improve, or retire.

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong product judgment across customer discovery, strategy, prioritization, experimentation, and tradeoffs.
  • Strong understanding of data products and how customers derive value from proprietary data and insights.
  • Practical understanding of modern machine learning and AI capabilities and limitations.
  • Working knowledge of applied data science and machine learning.
  • Ability to translate product requirements for Data Science and Engineering teams.
  • Familiarity with model evaluation concepts such as precision, recall, confidence, and model drift.
  • Ability to reason about probabilistic and imperfect data and define appropriate quality thresholds.
  • Strong analytical skills and ability to balance customer value, quality, coverage, cost, and speed.

Education and Experience

  • Experience partnering closely with Data Science and Engineering teams.

Success in This Role Looks Like

We use a structured interview process so every conversation has a distinct purpose and candidates are evaluated consistently against role-relevant evidence.

  1. Recruiter Prescreen — qualification and mutual fit. Confirm role basics, motivation, logistics, compensation alignment, and candidate priorities.
  2. Interview Round 1 — hiring-manager evidence interview. Evaluate the capabilities most predictive of success using consistent behavioral questions and anchored scoring.
  3. Interview Round 2 — work sample or functional deep dive. Explore the role’s most important on-the-job capabilities through a realistic, time-bounded discussion or exercise.
  4. Final Round — decision-gap interview. Assess any unresolved evidence required for a confident decision, such as cross-functional collaboration, judgment, leadership, or values in practice.

  • You operate as a true high-impact partner, collaborating effectively across teams and collaborators at all levels, bringing critical thinking and accountability to everything you do
  • You have a bias for action and thrive in ambiguity; you build the plan rather than waiting for one

jobs.description:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

  • Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

  • People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

  • Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical / engineering leadership interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

jobs.description:
About Wonderly

Wonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue. We serve the home service industry ($1.3T), and can consistently double a new customer’s revenue within 90 days. We make all of our AI and software completely free - and only get paid when our customers make real money. We’re here helping real small businesses make a life, pay for their children’s college tuition, and live the American dream.

Pre-AI SaaS sold tools. AI companies claim they sell outcomes - task done, call answered, lead booked, ticket resolved - but calls or leads aren’t the outcomes that ultimately matter. Revenue is what ultimately matters, and today, none of the AI companies actually promise revenue. Wonderly changes that.

Our 70-person team (mostly in PDE) spent over a year building in stealth; our thesis is that - if you actually want to control the end result (revenue) of a business and deploy AI fast/cheaply, you can’t just build the sexy part (agents), you must also build the unsexy parts and own everything end to end: the system of record layer and the application layer. We built from scratch every software a home service business needs - replacing ServiceTitan, Squarespace, Ringcentral, Jobber, Square, Hubspot, and a dozen others applications. And we built every agent necessary - AI marketing, AI receptionist, AI voice, AI sales outreach, AI sales coaching, AI follow-ups, AI 3D design, AI finance, AI quoting, AI collections, and more - all embedded inside our own system with native data access. As a result, we can deploy dozens of production-ready Agents to our customers in under 24 hours with no FDEs, no integrations, and no data cleaning work.

We are the most outcome driven business model in the business because we’ve proven our system and AI Agents actually work in driving the end result - revenue. We are not trying to sell our customers a dream - each of our 10+ core AI Agents help improve our customers’ revenue by 5-20%.

Wonderly already has PMF and has gone from 0 → 1 (we are happy to share more over a call), with very clear moat and deep industry knowledge that took a team of 70 hardcore A-players 18 months to build (we are at least 2 years ahead of anyone else in the space). We believe Wonderly has the potential to be a $100B - $1T outcome. The market is massive: home service businesses across North America (a $1.3T market). We’ve raised over $50M from top-tier investors, have $20M a year in free cashflow from another product line (Motion), and all that money gets pumped into Wonderly.

About the Hiring Manager

Hey, I’m Bishop, Head of Operations at Wonderly.

I’m extreme, direct, and care a lot about getting to the truth. I started in FP&A, realized I wanted to be in the middle of building something instead of analyzing it from the outside, and ended up here.

I work best with people who are high-agency, low-ego, and can handle intensity without needing a perfect playbook.

The Role

You’ll run the day-to-day of our inside sales team, the front line of how our contractors win jobs.

Our team works the leads we generate for our contractor customers, qualifies them fast, and books onsite appointments on the contractor’s behalf. Every lead that goes cold is money our customers lose, and money we lose. Your job is to make sure the team behind those bookings is staffed, trained, and performing every day.

That means:

  • Managing the team: schedules, coverage, weekend rotation, attendance

  • Hiring and onboarding new reps, and getting them productive fast

  • Listening to calls and coaching reps on what to fix

  • Tracking the numbers that matter (speed to lead, contact rate, booking rate, show rate) and acting when they slip

  • Handling performance issues directly, including the hard conversations

  • Keeping the process documented so the team doesn’t depend on any one person

  • Flagging what’s broken in the process so we can fix it, not just work around it

What Makes This Role Different

Most ops manager roles inherit a team that’s already built and a playbook that’s already set.

Here, the team is growing and the playbook is still being written. You’ll shape how the team is run, not just keep it running. If you see a better way to do coverage, coaching, or onboarding, you say it Monday and we’re testing it Wednesday.

You’ll work directly with me and Victoria, who leads Sales Operations, and you’ll see exactly how your decisions affect our customers’ revenue.

Backgrounds That Tend to Work

People from these backgrounds tend to thrive:

  • Running an inside sales or appointment-setting team

  • Team lead or sales floor manager who coached reps every day

  • Sales ops or support ops at a fast-growing company where you managed people, not just dashboards

  • Home services or remodeling companies where you ran the team that booked in-home appointments

Backgrounds we care less about:

  • Managers who have never sold or booked on the phone themselves

  • Ops or reporting roles with no people to manage

  • Account management or customer success with no team of your own

What matters more than the resume:

  • You’ve managed a team and been responsible for its numbers

  • You can listen to a call and know exactly what the rep should have done differently

  • You can have a hard conversation, say what needs to be said, and move on

  • You notice when something’s slipping before it shows up in the numbers

  • You’re organized, and you keep the team organized without being told twice

  • You’re comfortable with ambiguity and fast changes

Expectations

  • 60–70 hour weeks

  • Coverage that matches when leads come in, including some weekends

  • Real ownership of the team within your first 2 weeks

  • You own the team’s numbers and we’ll review them together regularly

  • The scope evolves constantly. As the team grows, so does the role.

Compensation

Total compensation: $130,000–$250,000 (base + equity)

Remote (US & Canada)

Wonderly is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone is treated with respect and given equal opportunities. We do not discriminate based on gender identity, race, ancestry, disability, religion, sexual orientation, pregnancy status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We welcome and encourage all qualified candidates to apply for our job openings.

jobs.title: Senior Accountant
jobs.excerpt: Put your accounting expertise to work.  Help shape what comes next.
jobs.description:
Put your accounting expertise to work. Help shape what comes next.

At Acuity Insights, we’re strengthening our accounting operations, improving our systems, and finding better ways to work. We’re looking for an experienced accountant who can take on complex work independently and help us build a stronger, more effective accounting function.

As our Senior Accountant, you’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, from close and financial reporting to revenue, reconciliations, and audit readiness. You’ll also help strengthen the accuracy and reliability of our financial and business reporting, including recurring revenue metrics, while contributing accounting insights to budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.

You’ll work closely with our Controller and alongside a small accounting team, bringing the judgment to work through complex accounting questions, identify root causes, and see issues through to resolution. Your experience will also help strengthen the team through shared knowledge, guidance, and better ways of working.

There’s plenty to improve and build. We’re preparing for a new accounting system, exploring automation and AI, and reducing the manual work that slows us down. You’ll have the opportunity to lead meaningful improvements while helping make our accounting processes more reliable and scalable.

If you enjoy solving complex accounting problems, sharing what you know, and finding better ways to get things done, there’s a lot here for you to contribute.

Before you apply: This is a fully remote role open to candidates anywhere in Canada. We’re hiring for an existing, open position. You’re welcome to use AI thoughtfully when preparing your application and conversations with our team. Just make sure what you share reflects your own experience, thinking, and judgment. During live conversations, please don’t use AI to generate responses unless invited to do so.

The Work You’ll Do

In your first few weeks, you’ll get to know Acuity’s business, current accounting systems, processes, and controls, working alongside our Controller and accounting team to understand how things work today and where we can improve.

We’re working toward a five-business-day close, and you’ll play an important role in helping us get there.

Own complex accounting work

You’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, including complex journal entries and reconciliations, month-end and year-end close, financial reporting, and audit support. You’ll also review reconciliations and supporting schedules prepared by the team, investigate unusual items, and ensure the close is complete and ready for Controller review.

When accounting questions are complex or something doesn’t reconcile, you’ll dig into the details, investigate root causes, and use sound judgment to recommend the right path forward. Your work will help us build a faster, more reliable close supported by strong processes and controls.

Strengthen revenue accounting and reporting

You’ll provide senior-level review and oversight of revenue accounting, including revenue recognition, deferred revenue, reconciliations, and related reporting. Working with teammates responsible for invoicing, receivables, and recurring revenue schedules, you’ll connect business activity with accounting records.

You’ll review accounting outputs, investigate discrepancies, and resolve complex or unusual transactions. You’ll help ensure revenue is recognized appropriately, supporting schedules reconcile to the general ledger, and financial and business reporting is accurate and reliable..

Turn accounting information into reliable financial insight

You’ll help ensure the accounting information behind our financial and business reporting is accurate, consistent, and reliable, including the preparation and reconciliation of recurring revenue metrics.

You’ll contribute accounting insights and historical context to financial analysis, budgeting, and forecasting, helping the business make informed decisions. You’ll also support cash management through short-term cash forecasting, cash flow variance analysis, and visibility into upcoming cash requirements.

Help modernize our accounting systems

We’re preparing to move to a new accounting platform. You’ll contribute your accounting expertise to the transition, from defining requirements and improving workflows to data validation, testing, and migration.

You’ll also have opportunities to take ownership of meaningful improvements that make our systems and processes more efficient, reliable, and easier to use.

Improve how Accounting works

You’ll look beyond your own responsibilities to identify recurring problems, unnecessary manual work, and opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen controls, and use automation or AI thoughtfully.

You’ll help turn those opportunities into practical improvements, while strengthening documentation, sharing knowledge, and building better coverage across the team.

The goal is an accounting function that spends less time moving information around and more time on the work where expertise and judgment matter.

Who You’ll Work With and How

You’ll report to our Controller and work alongside a small team of accountants. You’ll have meaningful ownership of your work while sharing knowledge, solving problems together, and helping strengthen how Accounting operates.

Accounting connects to almost every part of Acuity, so you’ll work closely with people across the business:

  • Your Accounting teammates, to work through complex questions, share expertise, strengthen coverage, and improve how the team works.
  • Revenue Operations, to connect contracts, billing, revenue, and the information that supports accurate financial reporting.
  • People & Culture, on payroll, employee-related accounting, and the processes that connect our teams.
  • Leaders and budget owners, to understand the context behind transactions, resolve accounting questions, and support reliable financial information.
  • External partners, including auditors and other Finance partners, to support reporting, compliance, and audit readiness.

You’ll work with a high degree of independence, but not in isolation. You’ll know when to make decisions, when to bring others in, and how to build trust through clear communication, sound judgment, and reliable follow-through.

What Success Looks Like

In your first three months, you’ll build an understanding of Acuity’s business, accounting cycle, systems, and controls. You’ll begin taking ownership of key accounting responsibilities, building relationships across the business, and identifying opportunities to improve how work gets done.

By six months, you’ll independently own significant areas of the accounting cycle, confidently work through complex reconciliations and accounting questions, and identify issues before they become problems. You’ll also begin turning improvement opportunities into practical changes.

By the end of your first year, you’ll be a trusted source of accounting expertise, handling complex work with minimal guidance and contributing improvements beyond your own responsibilities. Your impact will be visible in stronger processes, better controls, and greater shared knowledge and coverage across Accounting.

How You’ll Succeed

You’ll likely thrive here if you:

  • Take ownership. You follow work through to resolution, surface issues early, and take responsibility for accurate, reliable outcomes.
  • Look beyond the numbers. You investigate discrepancies, ask questions, and connect the dots to understand what’s really happening.
  • Balance judgment with momentum. You respect accounting standards and controls while knowing when to make decisions, move forward, or bring others in.
  • Look for better ways of working. You notice unnecessary complexity and manual effort, finding practical opportunities to improve processes, systems, and controls.
  • Share what you know. You document your work, offer guidance, and help build stronger knowledge and coverage across Accounting.
  • Use technology thoughtfully. You explore how systems, automation, and AI can improve your work, applying the same judgment and care you’d bring to any accounting decision.
  • Are comfortable building while doing. You work effectively as processes evolve, bringing structure to your own work while helping strengthen how Accounting operates.

As the Finance function evolves, you’ll have opportunities to deepen your expertise, take on broader ownership, and contribute to larger systems and process improvements.

Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running

You’ll bring strong technical accounting expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to independently own complex work. Your experience will include:

  • Independently owning significant areas of month-end and year-end close, including journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, working papers, and general ledger accounting.
  • Preparing or supporting financial reporting, ensuring the underlying accounting records are accurate, complete, and well supported.
  • Working across revenue recognition, invoicing, receivables, or other core accounting activities, with an understanding of how they connect through the accounting cycle.
  • Investigating complex accounting questions and discrepancies, applying accounting principles and professional judgment to determine the right path forward.
  • Supporting external audits and maintaining strong documentation, controls, and audit readiness.
  • Improving accounting processes, workflows, or systems to reduce manual work, strengthen reliability, and make the work more efficient.
  • Working independently in evolving environments, knowing when to make decisions, collaborate, or escalate.

Additional experience that would be valuable: Recurring revenue reporting, deferred revenue, budgeting, forecasting, cash management, or accounting system implementations.

Our current Finance systems include Xero, Dext, Airwallex, Plooto, and Stripe. You don’t need experience with these specific tools, but you should be comfortable working with cloud-based accounting systems and learning new technology.

A CPA designation, or progress toward one, is an asset but not required. Equivalent expertise developed through experience is equally valued.

How We Support You

  • Transparent compensation. A salary between $95,000 - $105,000 CAD, aligned to role scope, experience, and internal equity.
  • Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, whether that’s deepening your accounting expertise, building new technical skills, or exploring new areas of interest.
  • Shared success. Access to employee stock options, so you share in the value you help create.
  • Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.
  • Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.
  • Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.
  • Future-focused support. A 2% GRSP matching program to help you plan ahead.
  • Support for growing families. A 16-week parental leave top-up beyond EI, available to all parents.

What Happens After You Apply

We review every application carefully. Whether you apply directly, are referred, or connect through a recruiter or hiring manager, you’ll receive equal consideration.

We don’t use AI to evaluate applications, though you may be automatically screened out if you don’t meet baseline requirements (e.g. Canadian residency and valid work authorization). In some interviews, AI may help with note-taking, but all evaluations and decisions are made by real humans.

Our interviews are two-way conversations. We want to understand your career, abilities, and goals, and help you assess whether this opportunity and team are the right fit for you.

Steps in the Process

Our hiring process typically takes 2–4 weeks from initial conversation to final decision.

  • Application Review. A real person reviews your application for potential fit.
  • Intro Conversation. A conversation with a member of our Talent team to learn about your career journey, what you’re looking for next, and to introduce you to Acuity, Casper, and the role.
  • Conversation with the Manager. You’ll meet our Controller to explore the accounting work you’ve owned, how you approach complex problems, and the decisions you’ve made along the way. If you have an example of real work you’re proud of and can share, bring it along. It could be a process you’ve improved or a way you’ve used technology, automation, or AI to work more effectively. No need to prepare anything new or formal. It’s an opportunity to share how you approached the work, the judgment you applied, and what you learned.
  • Team Conversations. You’ll meet a few of the people you’d work with closely to explore how you collaborate, solve problems, and improve ways of working, while getting a better feel for what working together would be like.
  • Decision. The hiring manager reviews feedback from the interview team and typically makes a decision within 2 to 4 business days.
  • Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.

Life at Acuity Insights

We’re a remote-first team of 135+ people, built around trust, flexibility, and giving people meaningful ownership of their work.

Remote-first doesn’t mean working in isolation. We collaborate closely across teams, communicate thoughtfully across time zones, and create intentional opportunities to connect, while protecting the flexibility and focus that make remote work valuable.

Day to day, you can expect:

  • High trust and autonomy in how you get your work done.
  • Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team.
  • Opportunities to share ideas and perspectives that help inform our direction.
  • Colleagues who are generous with their expertise, challenge thinking, and learn from one another.
  • A culture of curiosity, continuous learning, and thoughtful experimentation, including how we use AI.
  • A sustainable approach to work that values impact over performative busyness.

As we grow, we’re deliberate about evolving how we work without adding process for process’s sake. We want people to have the clarity, context, relationships, and room to make good decisions, challenge assumptions, and contribute to work that matters.

About Acuity Insights

At Acuity Insights, we build research-backed technology that helps higher education institutions better understand people, make informed decisions, and support learner development.

We believe people are more than their grades, and that human potential can be understood, nurtured, and developed throughout the educational journey.

Our products support institutions and learners at different stages, from identifying potential and making fairer admissions decisions to supporting education, professional development, and growth. Our Casper situational judgment test, developed by researchers at McMaster University, has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is backed by nearly 20 years of research.

Today, we’re building toward a more connected ecosystem that brings together assessment, education, and development. By combining research, technology, and responsible AI, we aim to help institutions make better decisions, create more meaningful learning experiences, and support people in reaching their potential.

We’re at a point in our evolution where the work we do today is helping shape what’s possible tomorrow. And the people who join us will have an opportunity to contribute to that future.
