jobs.description:
Group Finance Director – Insurance & Investments

About the Role

The Group Finance Director is a senior leadership position responsible for overseeing the Group's financial management, planning, reporting, controls, treasury, and performance across its insurance, investment, asset management, and other financial services businesses.

The role provides strategic financial leadership across subsidiaries and business units, ensuring strong financial performance, regulatory compliance, capital discipline, effective risk management, and high-quality decision support for the Group CFO, CEO, Board, and shareholders.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Group-wide financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management.

Oversee consolidated financial reporting, management accounts, statutory accounts, and financial analysis across subsidiaries.

Drive FP&A, profitability analysis, cost optimization, and financial performance improvement.

Monitor financial performance across insurance, investments, asset management, and other Group businesses.

Oversee insurance finance, including premium revenue, claims, reserves, reinsurance, underwriting performance, and profitability analysis.

Lead financial reporting and accounting oversight for investment and asset management portfolios, including valuation, income, performance, and reporting.

Support Group-level capital planning, solvency, liquidity, and balance-sheet management.

Oversee treasury, cash management, funding requirements, and working-capital optimization.

Strengthen Group-wide financial controls, governance, policies, and risk management frameworks.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax requirements, insurance regulations, investment regulations, and statutory reporting obligations.

Provide financial analysis for M&A, joint ventures, strategic investments, restructuring, and capital allocation decisions.

Partner with senior executives to improve business-unit profitability, operating efficiency, and return on capital.

Lead finance transformation, including ERP, automation, management reporting, analytics, and digital finance initiatives.

Develop and mentor Finance Directors, Controllers, Heads of Finance, and senior finance teams across the Group.

Act as a key financial advisor to the Group CFO, CEO, Executive Committee, Board, auditors, regulators, investors, and other stakeholders.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Group revenue, EBITDA/profitability, and earnings growth

ROE / ROIC and return on capital

Budget and forecast accuracy

Cost-to-income and expense efficiency

Insurance underwriting and investment profitability

Capital adequacy and solvency position

Liquidity and treasury efficiency

Investment portfolio financial performance

Quality and timeliness of Group reporting

Regulatory and statutory compliance

Strength of internal controls and audit outcomes

Successful finance transformation and process automation

Value creation across subsidiaries and business units

Candidate Profile

15–20+ years of progressive finance experience, preferably within insurance, investment management, asset management, banking, pensions, reinsurance, or diversified financial services.

Proven experience operating at Group / regional / multi-entity level.

Previous experience as Group Finance Director, Finance Director, Group Financial Controller, Deputy Group CFO, Financial Controller, or senior finance executive.

Strong understanding of insurance accounting, investment accounting, financial reporting, capital management, treasury, and regulatory finance.

Demonstrated experience managing complex consolidated reporting structures and multiple subsidiaries.

Strong commercial understanding of investment portfolios, financial markets, capital allocation, and business performance.

Experience supporting M&A, corporate transactions, strategic investments, or restructuring is highly desirable.

Strong leadership experience managing geographically dispersed finance teams.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's/Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent is strongly preferred.

Additional qualifications in insurance, investment management, or financial risk are advantageous.

Core Competencies

Strategic Finance | Group Consolidation | FP&A | Financial Reporting | Insurance Finance | Investment Finance | Capital Management | Treasury | Solvency | Financial Controls | Regulatory Reporting | M&A | Risk Management | Tax | Finance Transformation | Investor & Board Reporting

Leadership Characteristics

Strategic and commercially minded

Strong analytical and financial judgment

High integrity and governance orientation

Excellent stakeholder and Board communication

Results-driven and performance-focused

Strong people leadership and succession-planning capability

Comfortable operating in complex, regulated, multi-entity environments

Reporting Line

Reports to: Group CFO / Group CEO

Key Stakeholders: Board of Directors, Executive Committee, Group CFO, CEOs/MDs of subsidiaries, Investment & Risk teams, Regulators, Auditors, Investors, and Shareholders.

Target Sourcing Titles

Group Finance Director | Group Financial Director | Group CFO | Deputy Group CFO | Finance Director | Group Financial Controller | Financial Controller | Regional Finance Director | Director of Finance | Head of Group Finance | Head of Finance | VP Finance | Deputy CFO | Finance Executive Director | Group Finance Controller

Who we are

Zus is a shared health data platform designed to accelerate healthcare data interoperability by providing easy-to-use patient data via API, embedded components, and direct EHR integrations. Founded in 2021 by Jonathan Bush, co-founder and former CEO of athenahealth, Zus partners with HIEs and other data networks to aggregate patient clinical history and then translates that history into user-friendly information at the point of care. Zus's mission is to catalyze healthcare's greatest inventors by maximizing the value of patient insights - so that they can build up, not around.

What we're looking for...

We’re looking for an experienced Staff Engineer to join the platform team at Zus which builds our core data services. The ideal candidate will be excited to take on the challenge of processing, storing and delivering the entire health records of millions of patients, providing low latency and high-availability for all operations. You are creative, innovative and think deeply about both the technical problems and business problems our customers are facing.

The Platform team has needed to rapidly innovate to stay ahead of data volumes that grow at 10x per year and a growing base of data-savvy customers using Zus to improve patient care. The team is also contending with an evolving regulatory landscape in data privacy and security. Expect to learn a lot and be put on mission-critical projects with direct customer impact.

The Platform team is at the heart of everything at Zus. You will work on data services that operate on large scale data using a variety of AWS services (Fargate, Lambda, DynamoDB, S3, etc) and use data storage technologies such as DynamoDB, postgres, iceberg, elasticsearch and others . You will also work on RESTful and GraphQL APIs that are used both internally and externally. Go is our language of choice and the team is responsible for deploying, maintaining, and operating its pipelines and services.

jobs.excerpt: The Role:We’re looking for a senior data engineer to own our data platform from architecture through production, reliably turning high volumes of data from provider APIs, webhooks, files, and web scraping into trusted records for our products.
jobs.description:
The Role:

We’re looking for a senior data engineer to own our data platform from architecture through production, reliably turning high volumes of data from provider APIs, webhooks, files, and web scraping into trusted records for our products.

Today, our enrichment and extraction workflows largely run serially inside a container. You’ll lead the move to a platform that supports concurrent processing, event-driven intake, and orchestrated batch workflows.

Responsibilities:

  • Multi-source intake: Build concurrent ingestion for provider APIs, webhooks, files, and scraping, with rate limits and failure handling.

  • Batch and event-driven execution: Orchestrate scheduled workflows and historical backfills using tools such as Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect. Build event-driven intake with Pub/Sub or Cloud Tasks, including retries, dead-letter queues, and controlled replay of failed work.

  • Raw-to-curated data: Preserve original payloads, including provider JSON, in Google Cloud Storage (GCS) before transforming them with dbt. Establish medallion layers for raw, standardized, and curated data.

  • Correctness through recovery: Implement idempotent upserts and safe retries, replay, and historical backfills that avoid duplicate records or data corruption. Make data traceable to its source and safe to reprocess.

  • Data quality and delivery: Define data contracts, build automated validation and pipeline tests, and monitor freshness and failures. Design and optimize PostgreSQL schemas, queries, and loading patterns so downstream products receive dependable data.

  • Extraction and enrichment: Integrate provider enrichment and LLM-based structured extraction from text into the platform.

Requirements:

  • Experience building multi-source production data platforms from zero to one, from initial architecture and pipeline implementation through deployment and ongoing operation.

  • Production experience with workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, or Temporal, including dependencies, retries, and failure recovery. Airflow experience is preferred.

  • Hands-on production experience with dbt and GCP.

  • Experience building event-driven systems with messaging or task queues, including asynchronous processing and failure recovery.

  • Strong SQL and PostgreSQL skills, including data modeling, query optimization, and reliable incremental loading. Experience with data contracts, raw and curated storage, retention policies, and automated quality checks.

  • Strong Python skills, including asynchronous HTTP and concurrent processing with tools such as asyncio, aiohttp, or HTTPX.

  • Hands-on web scraping experience with tools such as Scrapy, Playwright, Selenium, or Beautiful Soup, including concurrent scraping, rate limits, and failure handling.

Nice-to-Have:

  • Experience working in startups or small engineering teams, with broad ownership and changing priorities.

  • Entity resolution experience is especially valuable: matching company and people records across sources and reconciling duplicates into consistent entities.

  • LLM-based structured extraction or company and people data enrichment.

  • Familiarity with BigQuery and Dataform.

Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Senior RMF/ISSO Analyst to support Risk Management Framework, authorization, security-control assessment, and continuous-monitoring activities for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.

The RMF/ISSO Analyst will maintain authorization artifacts, control implementation statements, interconnection agreements, continuous-monitoring evidence, and system-level Plans of Action and Milestones. This role will support Tenant Security Plan compliance, Authority to Operate and Authority to Connect package reviews, security-control testing, and Security Test and Evaluation planning and execution.

The successful candidate will work with the Government Information System Security Manager, system owners, technical teams, assessors, and other cybersecurity stakeholders to resolve review comments and maintain complete, accurate, and traceable authorization evidence.

This position is remote, with a preference for candidates located in the Chicago area.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The RMF/ISSO Analyst will:

  • Maintain Risk Management Framework authorization packages and supporting documentation throughout the system authorization lifecycle.
  • Develop and maintain security-control implementation statements, control evidence, system security documentation, and continuous-monitoring records.
  • Maintain system-level Plans of Action and Milestones, including findings, remediation actions, milestones, responsible parties, supporting evidence, and closure status.
  • Develop, review, and maintain system interconnection agreements and related authorization documentation.
  • Support compliance with the USMEPCOM Tenant Security Plan for the organization’s portion of the DoD Information Network Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network.

  • Working knowledge of DoDI 8510.01, NIST SP 800-37, NIST SP 800-53, FISMA, and applicable DoD cybersecurity policies.

  • Experience developing and executing Security Test and Evaluation plans.
  • Experience conducting security-control assessments, control validation, evidence reviews, and authorization-readiness reviews.
  • Experience managing system-level POA&Ms and coordinating technical remediation activities.
  • Familiarity with ACAS or Tenable, STIG Viewer, SCAP tools, Endpoint Security Solutions, or comparable DoD cybersecurity technologies.
  • Experience maintaining traceable evidence repositories and resolving assessor or audit comments.
  • Additional certifications such as CGRC, CAP, CISM, CISSP, CASP+, or equivalent cybersecurity credentials.
  • Familiarity with current DoD 8140 cybersecurity workforce qualification requirements.
  • Strong technical writing, documentation management, analytical, and stakeholder-coordination skills.

jobs.excerpt: Who We AreImprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, , H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

Role Summary

We're looking for a Product Counsel, Data & Privacy to join our legal team as the first-line owner of data, privacy, and information-security legal work. Customer data is core to how Imprint's programs create value, and this role makes sure we share and protect that data the right way, advising on partner data sharing, privacy opt-outs, FCRA and credit data, GLBA/Reg P, data retention, and information security, while working at the pace of a startup that ships fast and takes its regulatory obligations seriously.

This is a high-ownership individual contributor role. You'll act as the first-line legal resource for data-sharing and privacy questions across our ongoing and launching programs. You'll have your own coverage areas from day one, direct access to senior leadership, and real influence on how customer data powers our products. You'll report to our Associate General Counsel and work alongside a small, experienced legal team, partnering closely with our Product Counsel, Data, and Security teams.

This role is ideal for a self-driven attorney who thrives in fast-moving environments, builds strong cross-functional relationships, and takes pride in owning work end-to-end.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Built strong working relationships with Data, Engineering, Security, and Compliance stakeholders.

  • Taken ownership of day-to-day data-sharing and privacy opt-out reviews that require legal sign-off.

  • Provided practical FCRA and GLBA/Reg P guidance on live matters and helped maintain the team's data-sharing and FCRA guides.

  • Advised on data retention questions and at least one partner information-security or incident-response matter.

  • Tracked and closed out legal requests with clear timelines and proactive communication to stakeholders.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the go-to legal advisor on partner data sharing: what customer, account, and application data can be shared through integrations and offline feeds, and on what legal basis, and document that guidance for the Data and business teams.

  • Advise on privacy opt-outs and suppression obligations, including processing partner privacy files and honoring opt-outs across data sets and downstream third parties; maintain business-facing data-sharing and opt-out guides.

  • Provide practical FCRA guidance, including permissible purpose, use and reuse of credit reports, and the sharing of application and credit-decision outcomes.

  • Advise on GLBA / Regulation P and consumer privacy notices, and draft, review, and maintain privacy notices and cardholder information-sharing notices.

  • Interpret state privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA and emerging state regimes) and automated-decision-making / AI requirements, and advise on their impact on data use, credit scoring, and product design.

  • Own data retention and deletion guidance: mapping regulatory retention obligations and destruction requirements and supporting the record-retention policy.

  • Partner with Security and GRC on partner and vendor information-security risk assessments, testing constraints, and incident response (including forensics, chain of custody, and breach/authority notification).

  • Provide product counseling to Product and Engineering on new features and builds that affect data sharing, privacy, or the customer experience, and draft the consents and data-related terms they need.

  • Coordinate with Compliance on regulatory interpretation, monitoring, and exam preparation, and support the Associate General Counsel on escalated complaints, regulatory inquiries, and bank-partner matters.

  • Translate complex data, privacy, and security requirements into clear, actionable guidance for cross-functional partners.

Qualifications

Required

  • J.D. from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing with at least one U.S. state bar.

  • 4 to 8 years in data privacy law, with demonstrated expertise in GLBA/Regulation P, FCRA, and state privacy laws including CCPA, and consumer financial regulation.

  • Experience in financial services, fintech, or a high-growth startup environment.

  • Working knowledge of FCRA and GLBA / Regulation P, and familiarity with state privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA and newer state regimes) and their practical application to data sharing and product.

  • Experience advising on data-sharing arrangements, privacy notices and opt-outs, and data retention.

  • Strong contract review skills, including data sharing agreements, DPAs, and regulatory-facing documentation.

  • Comfort partnering with security and information-security teams on vendor risk assessments, data protection, and incident response.

  • Demonstrated ability to work autonomously, own work end-to-end, manage competing priorities, and deliver clear legal guidance under tight timelines.

  • Strong communicator who proactively updates stakeholders and builds relationships across teams, able to explain a legal risk to an engineer, a data question to an analyst, and a regulatory nuance to a business leader with equal clarity.

  • Willingness to research independently and verify findings with senior team members.

Nice to Have

  • Privacy certification (e.g., CIPP/US).

  • Experience with FCRA in a lending or credit context, ECOA/Reg B adverse action, and automated decision-making / AI governance (e.g., state ADMT laws).

  • Familiarity with data-security frameworks (PCI DSS, SOC 2, NIST) and breach/incident-response processes.

  • Familiarity with additional consumer finance regulations (TILA/Reg Z, EFTA/Reg E, UDAAP, CAN-SPAM, TCPA) and their intersection with data and product.

  • Experience in sponsor bank, banking-as-a-service, or fintech partnership environments.

  • Experience with GDPR applicability and ROPA obligations.

  • Experience working in a ticketing or project management system (e.g., Linear, Jira, Asana).

  • Comfort with legal technology, AI-assisted workflows, and process automation.

  • Experience with consumer credit products, such as credit cards or buy-now-pay-later.

  • Experience building or standardizing privacy frameworks across multiple product lines or partner programs.

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents

  • Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

Imprint is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Imprint is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Imprint welcomes talented individuals from all backgrounds who want to build the future of payments and rewards. If you are passionate about FinTech and eager to grow, let’s move the world forward, together.

Compensation Range: $200K - $250K

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Role

We're looking for a Lead Site Reliability Engineer to build and run the fundamental part of Nebius in APAC: the Network, the infrastructure everything else depends on. We are at the early stage of our APAC expansion, so this is a hands-on role. You will define reliability targets, write automation and handle incidents yourself, with a high degree of independence from the European teams. As the region grows, you will build and lead the local SRE team.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Define and own reliability goals for network services and critical paths in the region (SLIs/SLOs, availability targets, error budgets where it makes sense)
  • Drive reliability improvements across the whole APAC network: not only services, but also site readiness, inter-site connectivity (DCI), and operational standards for new data centers
  • Own incident response for your areas, lead investigations/postmortems, and turn failures into durable fixes (not repeated firefighting); set up on-call and incident management practices for the region
  • Build and evolve observability: actionable metrics/logs/traces, alerting, and faster debug loops during and after incidents
  • Design safer change workflows: automation, CI/CD, test/staging environments, canarying, rollbacks, and auditability for network changes
  • Work closely with network engineers and platform teams in APAC and Europe to embed operability into designs and keep operations practical and fast
  • Hire, onboard and mentor the first SREs in the region and set the engineering bar for the team
  • Coordinate with European teams on handoffs and coverage across time zones

We expect you to have:

  • 7+ years of experience in SRE / infrastructure engineering, including experience leading a team or acting as a technical lead with broad ownership of production systems
  • Strong production Linux fundamentals and a structured approach to debugging complex systems
  • Solid understanding of networking basics and how real networks fail (control plane vs data plane, latency/loss, failure domains, etc.)
  • Hands-on experience operating high-availability systems and improving them over time (not just "keeping lights on")
  • Ability to write and maintain software/automation (Go is common for us; Python is also welcome)
  • Experience with modern infrastructure tooling (e.g., IaC, CI/CD, container platforms) and comfort automating operational workflows
  • Ability to work independently in an early-stage environment and to build processes and a team from scratch
  • Willingness to stay hands-on while leading and growing a team

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Experience with high-throughput traffic processing: load balancers, tunneling/decap, NAT64, or similar datapath-heavy systems
  • Low-level networking performance/debug background (eBPF/XDP, DPDK, perf/ftrace, kernel networking internals)
  • Experience building network-safe delivery pipelines (testing labs, staged rollouts, automated verification, drift detection)
  • Background with large-scale network observability/telemetry (routing/flow telemetry, regression detection at scale)
  • Knowledge of the APAC network landscape (carriers, IX, regional connectivity and regulatory specifics)

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

  • Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

  • People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

  • Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical / engineering leadership interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

What We Can Achieve Together:

The Senior BI Analyst executes design and implementation of creative and effective data solutions to fulfill the requirements and strategic objectives of Conservancy business areas such as Finance, Human Resources, and Conservation programs. This is a highly collaborative role combining technical expertise and partnership acumen to provide guidance and recommendations in the strategic use of integrated data to illuminate insights and accelerate Conservancy impact. The Senior BI Analyst is technical lead on analytics projects of varying scope and complexity, and subject matter expert in their domains. They make recommendations that improve and strengthen end products and actively advance the Conservancy's application of AI-enhanced analytics solutions to improve efficiency, ensure scalability, and encourage a culture of data-driven decisions.

The Senior BI Analyst maintains and enhances a robust Power BI relational model of conservation program and financial data and metrics to ensure accuracy and functional integrity for measuring conservation progress against goals and financial components. The Senior BI Analyst designs and implements technical and process solutions, including activities such as investigating specific business questions, building enterprise dashboards, and delivering self-service analytics resources that empower business users.

We’re Looking for You:

We’re looking for a curious, results-driven, and team-oriented technical leader who is passionate about data and meticulous about accuracy. The successful candidate is inspired by technical challenges, persistent about effective solutions, and dedicated to continuous improvement of team products and processes. They are a self-starter that thrives in an agile execution environment focused on iteration and responsiveness and are motivated to empower business partners to explore and analyze enterprise data. The successful candidate is dedicated to staying current on analytics industry advancements and new technologies and evaluating them for potential benefits to the Conservancy. This position is open remote in US.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline and 5 years’ experience in programming and systems design, or equivalent combination.

  • Proficiency with SQL, Databricks (DB SQL), M, DAX or similar language and data manipulation concepts (e.g., table joins, cardinality).

  • Experience building visualizations and dashboards with Microsoft Power BI, AWS Quick Sight, or similar BI tool.

  • Experience leading multi-disciplinary project teams to design, document, and implement fit for purpose technical solutions, including communicating technical concepts to non-technical and leadership audiences.

  • Experience soliciting business requirements and translating desired business outcomes into technical specifications for engineering partners.

  • Experience with enterprise self-service paradigm, including data literacy enablement, and data governance principles.

  • Experience independently prioritizing multiple competing demands in a fast-paced environment.

  • Excellent written and oral communication skills and exceptional customer services skills.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience analyzing complex system-wide technical specifications and interfaces, troubleshooting and debugging data products, and producing effective user and technical documentation.

  • Experience working with relational databases, data modeling, data warehousing, and data governance.

  • Experience incorporating AI tools, such as machine‑learning platforms, natural‑language processing tools, or automation frameworks into analytical workflows.

The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $85,000 – $125,000. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer.Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

IT Operations Manager


Position Summary

The IT Operations Manager provides strategic and operational leadership for enterprise technology services supporting mission-critical programs, grants management, volunteer service initiatives, disaster response activities, and agency business operations. This role oversees day-to-day IT operations while serving as a senior technical advisor responsible for cloud infrastructure, enterprise applications, cybersecurity coordination, change management, operational governance, and modernization initiatives.

The position requires a blend of leadership, technical expertise, project management, and stakeholder engagement to ensure secure, reliable, and compliant technology services.


Key Responsibilities

IT Operations Leadership

  • Direct and coordinate daily IT service delivery across infrastructure, cloud services, enterprise applications, identity management, and end-user support.
  • Establish operational priorities, resource allocations, and service delivery expectations.
  • Lead operational reviews and status meetings while monitoring project and program performance.
  • Ensure operational activities align with strategic goals and mission requirements.
  • Serve as escalation point for operational issues, outages, and service disruptions.

Cloud and Infrastructure Management

  • Provide leadership for Microsoft Azure and cloud modernization initiatives.
  • Oversee cloud infrastructure deployments, networking, platform services, storage, databases, and identity services.
  • Coordinate environment provisioning, production releases, and operational readiness reviews.
  • Ensure solutions comply with federal security and architecture requirements.

Enterprise Applications and Business Systems

  • Support operational management of enterprise applications including:
    • ServiceNow
    • Azure DevOps
    • Microsoft 365
    • Custom mission support applications
  • Review application onboarding requests and operational impacts.
  • Coordinate application lifecycle management and production support activities.
  • Support governance decisions regarding application hosting and enterprise integration strategies.

Change, Release, and Governance Management

  • Lead Change Advisory Board (CAB) activities and operational governance processes.
  • Review technical change requests for risk, compliance, operational impact, and implementation readiness.
  • Coordinate stakeholders, technical teams, and agency leadership during change planning and execution.
  • Ensure accurate documentation, implementation plans, testing procedures, and rollback strategies.
  • Promote successful change adoption across the organization.

Cybersecurity and Compliance

  • Partner with agency cybersecurity teams to maintain a secure and compliant operating environment.
  • Support Security Impact Assessments (SIAs), Authority to Operate (ATO) activities, and audit responses.
  • Evaluate operational risks associated with new applications, integrations, and cloud services.
  • Ensure compliance with federal security requirements, FISMA controls, and agency governance policies.
  • Participate in incident response and security remediation activities.

Program Support and Disaster Response Technology

  • Support technology platforms that enable client’s programs and mission operations.
  • Coordinate IT services supporting disaster services initiatives and emergency response capabilities.
  • Ensure operational readiness of systems that support program delivery and field activities.
  • Collaborate with program offices to align technology investments with agency priorities.

Vendor, Contractor, and Team Leadership

  • Manage and mentor technical staff, contractors, and service providers.
  • Coordinate work across engineering, operations, cybersecurity, networking, and application support teams.
  • Support workforce planning, onboarding, performance management, and training initiatives.
  • Foster collaboration and accountability among cross-functional teams.

Strategic Planning and Modernization

  • Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency through automation and process improvement.
  • Lead modernization initiatives involving cloud adoption, security enhancement, and service transformation.
  • Provide recommendations to leadership on technology investments and operational improvements.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and industry best practices for agency adoption.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field.
  • 8+ years of progressive IT experience.
  • 3+ years in operational leadership, management, or supervisory roles.
  • Experience supporting federal government information systems.
  • Demonstrated expertise with:
    • Microsoft Azure
    • Microsoft 365
    • Identity and Access Management
    • ServiceNow
    • Cloud Operations
    • Enterprise Application Support
    • Change Management
  • Experience leading cross-functional operational teams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting federal civilian agencies.

  • Knowledge of federal cybersecurity frameworks and compliance requirements.
  • Experience supporting Disaster Services, Grants Management, Volunteer Programs, or Mission Support systems.
  • ITIL, PMP, Microsoft Azure, CISSP, or related certifications.

jobs.title: Growth Marketing Lead
jobs.excerpt: Who We AreImprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, , H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

The Role

We're looking for a Growth Marketing Lead to grow new cardholder accounts across Imprint's partner credit card programs. The Growth Marketing Lead owns credit card acquisition across prescreen and invitation-to-apply (ITA) direct mail, card marketplaces and affiliates, paid search, paid social, and third-party email. The role is responsible for building these channels from an early stage, establishing operating infrastructure, vendor and bureau relationships, measurement frameworks, and repeatable execution processes, while delivering against approved account, cost per account, and credit quality targets.

The role works closely with Risk and Credit. Targeting, offer, and channel decisions affect approval rates, credit performance, and program economics, and the Growth Marketing Lead is accountable for balancing acquisition volume with account quality.

This is a senior individual contributor role. The Growth Marketing Lead operates through a combination of direct hands-on execution and external agency and vendor management. Budget recommendations are developed by this role and presented to General Managers and Finance for approval. Approved budgets are then managed and allocated by this role across channels and partners.

This role reports to the VP of Marketing.

Responsibilities

Acquisition Strategy & Planning

  • Own credit card acquisition strategy across prescreen and ITA direct mail, card marketplaces, affiliates, paid search, paid social, and third-party email

  • Translate GTM and partner objectives into acquisition plans covering target segments, channel mix, offers, flighting, budget recommendations, creative requirements, and KPIs

  • Develop budget recommendations for GM and Finance review, with expected approved accounts, cost per approved account, and payback by channel

  • Allocate approved budgets across channels and partners to maximize approved account volume within cost and credit quality targets

  • Partner with GMs and Product to test welcome offers and partner reward structures by segment and channel

  • Run the channel layer of Imprint's acquisition engine, which combines partner, Imprint, and bureau data to decide which prospect receives which partner offer, through which channel, and when

  • Build and maintain acquisition playbooks and operating standards so new partner programs launch with owned acquisition channels ready

  • Establish an operating cadence across partners: intake, planning, launch, optimization, and reporting, with defined roles, SLAs, and measurement standards

Prescreen & ITA Direct Mail

  • Own Imprint's prescreen and ITA direct mail programs, including strategy, audience selection, offers, creative direction, vendor management, and performance measurement

  • Define prescreen criteria with Risk to balance response rate, approval rate, and early credit performance

  • Manage relationships with credit bureaus, list vendors, and print and mail production partners

  • Ensure all prescreen campaigns comply with FCRA firm offer and opt-out notice requirements, coordinating with Legal, Compliance, and our issuing bank partners

  • Build and maintain the measurement framework for direct mail, including holdout testing and tracking each campaign through response, approval, activation, and early delinquency

Card Marketplaces & Affiliates

  • Own Imprint's presence on card marketplaces and comparison sites such as Credit Karma, NerdWallet, and Experian, including pre-qualified offer integrations

  • Manage affiliate platform operations, publisher onboarding, commission structures tied to approved accounts, and fraud and quality controls

  • Identify and develop new marketplace and affiliate partnerships aligned with Imprint's target cardholder profile

  • Ensure publisher creative and offer claims comply with partner brand standards, TILA/Reg Z disclosure requirements, and UDAAP

Paid Digital & Third-Party Email

  • Manage day-to-day execution across paid search, paid social, and third-party email through a mix of direct hands-on work and agency management

  • Optimize channels to approved accounts, including audience targeting, bid strategy, creative iteration, suppression and eligibility logic, and landing page coordination

  • Use partner first-party data, such as loyalty members and app users, for targeting, lookalikes, and suppression within each partner's data-sharing terms

  • Partner with Product and Design to reduce drop-off across the application funnel, from landing page to submitted application to approval

  • Ensure all channel activity meets Imprint's compliance, issuing bank, and partner brand standards

Measurement & Reporting

  • Partner with Analytics to define attribution and incrementality measurement that separates owned channel acquisition from partner channel and organic volume

  • Build and maintain acquisition dashboards and weekly reporting by channel and partner, tracking spend through approved accounts, activation, early spend, and early credit performance, with clear insights and recommended actions

  • Design and execute a structured creative and offer testing program in partnership with Creative, including brief development, variant design, readout cadence, and iteration

  • Partner with Lifecycle to coordinate suppression of existing cardholders and open applicants, frequency management, and the handoff from acquisition into onboarding programs

KPIs

  • Approved accounts by channel and partner

  • Cost per approved account by channel and partner

  • Cost per acquired, activated cardholder (CAC)

  • Approval rate and first-transaction activation rate by channel

  • Early spend and early delinquency by channel

  • Cost per application and application volume as funnel diagnostics

  • Direct mail response rate and cost per response

  • Marketplace and affiliate contribution to approved accounts

  • Channel incrementality where measurable

Qualifications

Required

  • 7 to 10+ years of performance or direct marketing experience with direct ownership of credit card or consumer lending acquisition channels and budgets

  • Hands-on experience running prescreen or ITA direct mail programs, including credit bureau and list vendor relationships

  • Demonstrated track record of growing approved account volume while improving cost per account and maintaining credit quality, working directly with Credit and Risk teams

  • Working knowledge of credit card marketing regulation, including FCRA, TILA/Reg Z, UDAAP, and ECOA/Reg B, and experience moving creative through Legal, Compliance, and bank review

  • Hands-on expertise across at least two of: paid search, paid social, affiliates and card marketplaces, direct mail. Working knowledge across all four preferred

  • Experience managing a combination of direct execution and agency or vendor relationships

  • Strong analytical capability: card acquisition economics, attribution modeling, funnel diagnostics, cohort analysis, and holdout testing

  • Experience building operating processes, including cadences, SLAs, and playbooks, in addition to running campaigns

  • Ability to operate effectively in a multi-partner environment where acquisition programs must balance partner-specific requirements with scalable infrastructure

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to present budget recommendations and performance results to senior commercial stakeholders

Nice to Have

  • Co-branded credit card experience at an issuer, program manager, or brand partner

  • Experience with pre-qualified offer programs on card marketplaces such as Credit Karma Lightbox or Experian Activate

  • Experience building response and approval models in partnership with Data Science

  • Familiarity with incrementality testing or media mix modeling

  • Experience coordinating with CRM and lifecycle teams on suppression and frequency management

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents

  • Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

Imprint is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Imprint is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Imprint welcomes talented individuals from all backgrounds who want to build the future of payments and rewards. If you are passionate about FinTech and eager to grow, let’s move the world forward, together.

Compensation Range: $175K - $200K

jobs.description:
The Marketing Director is Myo's senior marketing leader responsible for setting the strategic direction of the marketing function, owning the performance of paid acquisition and lifecycle programs, and actively developing the capabilities of the marketing team.

Myo’s marketing team is lean and scrappy. This is a hands-on leader who sets the bar by doing. The right person has built and shaped marketing functions before. They know how a marketing team should operate at different stages of a business, how to distinguish between what needs immediate attention and what is working well enough to leave alone, and how to make the case for marketing investments (including those without a clean attribution story) with conviction and intellectual honesty. They bring enough depth across paid media, lifecycle, launch strategy, and brand to answer most tactical questions from experience. They use AI to move faster and cover more ground, and they actively share how they think so the people around them get sharper over time.

Essential Role Functions

Growth, Acquisition & Retention Strategy

  • Owns Myo's paid media program (Meta and Google Ads) across Canada and the US: strategy, testing agenda, creative briefs and channel structure. Tests additional paid channels and creative formats (TikTok, YouTube, etc.).
  • Sets content strategy and creative direction across organic social, short-form video, and search (including visibility in AI search), with a clear point of view on how Myo wins on each.
  • Diagnoses account performance personally, decides what to test next, and flags spend that isn't working.
  • Leads the full marketing launch for each new clinic and improves the playbook so each launch goes better than the last.
  • Owns lifecycle and retention strategy: welcome, early retention, post-visit follow-up, and win-back. Accountable for measurable improvement in first-30-day retention.

Measurement & Investment

  • Owns the performance dashboard and the monthly channel read. Explains why results moved and brings a recommendation, not just the numbers.
  • Owns marketing budget allocation across the full mix: campaign type, channel, funnel stage, and investment type, using performance data to shift spend toward the highest-returning mix.
  • Sets success criteria before tests begin, reads results honestly, and reallocates budget based on results.

Team Leadership & Function Building

  • Leads the marketing team by example and manages agencies, contractors and vendors, including decisions on those relationships.
  • Embeds AI across the marketing workflow (creative production, analysis and reporting, lifecycle, prototyping, etc.) by building and using the workflows personally, then teaching the team to do the same.
  • Decides what needs focus and what should be systematized, maintained, or left alone, and builds the structure that lets creative work happen without disrupting priority execution.
  • Develops the team's judgment by sharing the thinking behind where to push, what to protect, how to argue for investment, and where to allocate attention.
  • Runs the weekly rhythm that keeps priorities clear, work visible and decisions moving.

Measures of Success

  • New client acquisition volume grows quarter over quarter.
  • Paid media CAC trends in the right direction, not because spend decreased, but because targeting, creative, and channel decisions improved.
  • First 30-day new client retention improves.
  • New clinic openings hit their presale and early-volume targets.
  • Brand and non-performance marketing investments are argued for clearly before funding and are tracked against success criteria.
  • A performance dashboard exists that any senior stakeholder can read in 10 minutes and understand channel health.
  • The marketing team demonstrates measurably stronger judgment over time, evidenced by improved independent decision-making.
  • AI-enabled workflows are in production across the team, with measurable gains in speed or output.

Role Competencies

  • Hands-on leadership: You’re a player-coach. You’re comfortable doing the work yourself and leading a small team by example.
  • Paid media fluency: You've managed meaningful Meta and Google budgets and can diagnose performance issues and evaluate account health firsthand.
  • AI fluency: You build and use AI workflows to work faster and cover more ground without lowering the quality bar.
  • Function-building experience: You've shaped a marketing team, and you know what good looks like at different stages of a business.
  • Investment judgment: You run clean experiments, stay skeptical of vanity metrics, balance data with intuition, and can make an honest case for spend, including brand work without clean attribution.
  • Content point of view: You have strong, defensible opinions on what wins on social and in search, and can brief and critique creative at a high level.
  • Teaching orientation: You build capability in the team, not dependency on yourself.
  • Brand and category fluency: You protect Myo's premium positioning and know that trust and education convert better than urgency here.

Core Values To Live By

  • Care Deeply. (Empathy)
  • One Team, One Dream. (Collaboration)
  • Make it Count. (Focus)
  • Set the Pace. (Ambition)
  • Never Stop Learning. (Curiosity)

We're looking for an Account Executive who knows eCommerce and shipping, runs a tight sales process, and loves the work of discovery, demo, and close. Our mission is bold: To design and deliver research and evidence-based approaches to eliminate the gaps between young children's inherent potential and their achievement in school and life. As the Account Executive, HELP at Shine Early Learning, you will own the management and growth of the Hawaii Early Learning Profile (HELP) product suite. HELP is a comprehensive birth-to-3 development assessment suite encompassing print materials, HELP Connect (a digital assessment platform), and associated training and certification offerings.

As Account Executive, you will be responsible for both account management and new business development across a diverse customer base including Early Intervention service providers, Early Childhood Education providers, Early Head Start providers, and relevant local, regional, and state agencies. You will be responsible for delivering new customer acquisition, as well as account expansion by migrating customers from print to HELP Connect, and expanding adoption of training and certification offerings.

Our ideal candidate is passionate about supporting the development of children from birth to age three and brings hands-on experience in Early Intervention, Early Childhood Education, or a related field. They understand the needs of practitioners and programs serving young children and are excited to help customers use HELP more effectively to improve outcomes. We are looking for someone who is relationship-oriented, consultative, entrepreneurial, and motivated to grow the reach and impact of HELP. Prior sales experience is not required, but candidates must be comfortable with the commercial aspects of the role, including building customer relationships, identifying growth opportunities, and being accountable for revenue targets.

This role reports to the Chief Growth Officer and operates as an individual contributor, with the potential to build and lead a larger team as the business scales.


Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

One of the top benefits of working at PartsBase is the culture. We are a TEAM-focused organization, and everyone celebrates each other's successes. Our inclusive culture welcomes all employees and values their unique contributions to our success. Our clients tell us time and time again that our people set us apart from the competition. We naturally strive to hire the very best talent. The ideal candidate is a motivated, well-organized individual who has a deep understanding of prospecting and developing strong relationships with customers.

Role Overview

PartsBase is seeking an accomplished Controller to serve as the company's senior technical authority in accounting, financial reporting, tax, and audit. This is a hands-on, player-coach role: the Controller will supervise and closely review the work of the accounting team, own the company's core accounting, reporting, and tax provision deliverables, and partner directly with the Chief Operating Officer, the Director of Finance and Operations, and executive leadership. This role will raise the quality, completeness, and documentation of the close, consolidate all entities on a consistent GAAP basis, and prepare the company for its first financial statement audit.

The ideal candidate brings more than 10 years of progressive accounting and finance experience, deep expertise in tax and audit, and a forward-looking approach to applying AI and automation to strengthen the accuracy, efficiency, and scalability of the finance function.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the company's subject matter expert on U.S. GAAP, technical accounting, and accounting policy, providing authoritative guidance to Finance and business leaders

  • Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close, including journal entries, account reconciliations, flux analyses, and GAAP-compliant financial statements

  • Supervise and review, in close detail, the accounting work of the team across accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll and benefits, commissions, and intercompany reconciliations, including journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, supporting documentation, and flux analysis, with appropriate segregation of duties

  • Own the federal and state income tax provision under ASC 740, prepared quarterly and at year end beginning with 12/31/2026; review federal and state tax returns prepared by external preparers for accuracy and compliance rather than relying on the preparers; and own sales/use tax nexus, indirect tax, and state and international tax considerations, coordinating with external tax advisors

  • Build audit readiness ahead of the company's first financial statement audit, including prepared-by-client schedules and workpapers, and serve as the primary liaison to external auditors once engaged

  • Own revenue accounting under ASC 606 for SaaS and subscription arrangements, which make up the large majority of company revenue, as well as PBExpo event revenue and PartStore, along with deferred revenue, accruals, and prepaid expenses

  • Own multi-entity accounting and consolidation, including review of the PBExpo cash-basis to accrual conversion, intercompany reconciliations and eliminations, and related-party transactions

  • Write and maintain revenue recognition and technical accounting policy memos, and establish accounting policies for business operations

  • Monitor, assess, and implement new and emerging accounting standards

  • Design, document, and maintain a strong internal control environment, including accounting policies and procedures that support audit and compliance requirements

This role is expected to hold the SMF16 (Compliance Oversight) Senior Management Function once approved, and will act as our primary point of contact with the FCA.

This is a build role: you'll be creating frameworks, policies, and controls from scratch rather than inheriting an existing function.

Why This Role Matters

The Director of Compliance and Risk (UK) will:

  • Design and enforce compliance frameworks that enable safe scaling of digital financial services.

  • Ensure BJAK operates in accordance with UK regulatory standards, especially FCA requirements.

  • Protect consumers through transparent, fair, and ethical practices.

  • Establish BJAK as a trusted partner with regulators, partners, and industry stakeholders.

What You Will Do

Regulatory Leadership & Strategy

  • Develop and maintain compliance frameworks aligned with UK regulatory requirements.

  • Lead regulatory readiness for market entry, licensing, and ongoing supervision.

  • Serve as the primary contact with the FCA and relevant UK bodies.

  • Interpret regulatory changes and guide business strategy accordingly.

Risk Governance & Compliance Operations

  • Build policies and controls covering AML, KYC, data privacy, consumer duty, distribution, and claims-related compliance.

  • Conduct risk assessments and implement remediation plans for identified gaps.

  • Establish monitoring, testing, and reporting processes for ongoing compliance.

  • Ensure internal audits, compliance reviews, and control testing are operationalised.

Consumer Protection & Business Integrity

  • Embed fairness, transparency, and responsible selling throughout the organisation.

  • Oversee product compliance, marketing reviews, pricing governance, and distribution oversight.

  • Implement complaint handling frameworks aligned with regulatory standards.

Cross-Functional Support & Training

  • Partner with product, operations, legal, marketing, and commercial teams to ensure compliant execution.

  • Provide guidance on regulatory implications of new products, partnerships, or distribution models.

  • Deliver training to ensure teams understand and execute compliance responsibilities.

You Will Thrive in This Role If You

  • See compliance as a strategic enabler, not a blocker.

  • Operate with high integrity, sound judgment, and strong attention to detail.

  • Communicate clearly and influence leaders using data and logic.

  • Enjoy building frameworks and scaling systems from early-stage to mature environments.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, evolving settings where regulation meets innovation.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of compliance, risk, or regulatory experience within financial services, insurance, insurtech, or fintech.

  • Deep understanding of UK regulatory frameworks, including FCA rules and consumer duty requirements.

  • Experience in compliance for digital platforms, distribution, or insurance products (preferred).

  • Background in insurtech, digital distribution, or online marketplaces.

Location Requirement

Why Join Us

  • Build frameworks that enable safe, inclusive financial access at scale.

  • Work closely with leadership and regulators to drive responsible innovation.

  • Competitive compensation with long-term growth and international career opportunities.
