Job Description

The Regional Medical Scientific Director (RMSD) - Cardiovascular & Metabolism is a credentialed (i.e., PhD, PharmD, DNP, MD) therapeutic and disease expert who engages in scientific exchange with leaders in the external medical and scientific community. RMSDs provide to Scientific Leaders (SLs) balanced, factual, scientific information about non-product areas of interest to the company. RMSDs reply to scientific questions from SLs, including questions about company products. The work of an RMSD is aligned to the core pillars: Scientific Exchange, Clinical Research, Scientific Congress Support, and Scientific Insights. This position covers the territory of Michigan & Northern Ohio.


Scientific Exchange:

  • Develop professional relationships and engage with national and regional Urology SLs to ensure access to medical and scientific information on areas of therapeutic interest and company products.
  • Conduct peer-to-peer scientific discussions and maintain a reliable presence with those SLs to ensure they have a medical contact within the company.
  • Address scientific questions and direct SL inquiries on issues outside of RMSD scope (e.g. grants) to appropriate company resources consistent with applicable policies.
  • Review HQ-directed education and training to maintain current knowledge and comprehension of dynamic scientific and clinical environment in the company's areas of interest.

*Scientific exchange does not include promotional claims about any drug, vaccine or biologic product. RMSDs have no sales objectives or accountability for prescribing or sales of any company product and are required to avoid any situations that could create the appearance that they have such responsibilities. A RMSD may not comment on or make suggestions with respect to the diagnosis, treatment, or circumstances of a specific patient.


Clinical Research:

  • Liaison between the scientific community and company to enhance the comprehension of scientific foundations and goals for approved, in development and active Company-Sponsored Trials and/or our Company's Investigator-Sponsored Program (MISP) research studies.

Upon request from Global Clinical Trial Operations (GCTO):

  • Identify barriers to patient enrollment and retention efforts to achieve study milestones, recommend study sites, and identify potential investigators to participate in phase II-IV clinical development programs.
  • Address questions from investigators and provide information regarding participation in our Company-sponsored clinical studies.

Upon request from Global Center for Scientific Affairs (GCSA):

  • Enhance the comprehension of the scientific foundations and goals of our company Investigator Studies Program (MISP) research.
  • Identify barriers to patient enrollment and retention efforts to achieve study milestones.
  • Initiate discussions with SLs and/or potential investigators that include scientific/data exchange within our Areas of Interest (AOIs) to determine the alignment with our research strategies, study concepts, scientific merit, and qualifications for a specific compound or trial.

Scientific Congresses:

  • Engage in scientific and medical meetings through pre-congress preparation, facilitate scientific and data exchange for both our Company and competitor data, collect meaningful insights, and staff congress exhibit booth as applicable.

Scientific Insights:

  • Gather feedback, data, or information during routine activities that can help the company better comprehend medical or scientific needs, priorities, or concerns of healthcare practitioners and/or patients.

Scientific Excellence:

  • Serve as a role model for other field medical team members, including on-boarding and/or therapeutic training.

Location:

  • This is a remote position that serves the territory of Michigan & Northern Ohio. This person must reside in the territory.
  • Ability to travel up to 50%

Education Minimum Requirement:

  • PhD, PharmD, DNP, or MD.

Required Experience and Skills:

  • Proven competence and a minimum of 3 years of relevant therapeutic area (Cardiovascular & Metabolism) experience beyond that obtained in the terminal degree program, e.g., Atherosclerosis / Lipidology / MASH (metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis).
  • Ability to conduct doctoral-level discussions with key external stakeholders
  • Dedication to scientific excellence with a strong focus on scientific education and dialogue
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and networking skills
  • A thorough comprehension of FDA, OIG, HIPAA, and other ethical guidelines, laws, and regulations relevant to the pharmaceutical industry and its customers
  • Ability to organize, prioritize, and work effectively in a constantly changing environment
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams, OneNote)
  • Familiarity with virtual meeting platforms

Desire to contribute to a positive and collaborative work environment by:


  • Working to transform the environment, culture, and business landscape
  • Leveraging varied perspectives and experiences to ensure business value, consistent with the global people strategy
  • Ensuring accountability to drive an inclusive culture
  • Strengthening the foundational elements of talent and teamwork
  • Consistent adherence to field and corporate policies and Global Medical Scientific Affairs (GMSA) strategy, including field standard operating procedures (SOPs), Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines, and administrative/operational responsibilities

Preferred

Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

  • Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

  • People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

  • Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical / engineering leadership interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Operations
jobs.excerpt: Alternative Payments is building the financial operating system for SMBs, consolidating the disconnected tech stack that holds service-based businesses back.
jobs.description:
Alternative Payments is building the financial operating system for SMBs, consolidating the disconnected tech stack that holds service-based businesses back. Starting with MSPs, we've spent five years perfecting accounts receivable, and we're now expanding into accounts payable, AI-powered analytics, and beyond. We're at an inflection point: closing the loop on money movement and laying the foundation for a platform that will reshape how service businesses operate financially.

We're growing fast, thinking big, and building a global team that wants to be part of something that lasts. We believe the best solutions come from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and a shared obsession with customer impact. If you're energized by real problems, real customers, and real impact, we want to hear from you!

Why should you apply for this role?

We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer who can take a real business problem, understand why it matters, and build the system that solves it. You'll own initiatives end to end, partner closely with operations, data, and product, and explore net-new product POCs and build internal tooling, automations and AI agents / agentic workflows that help the whole company move faster.

This is an internal-facing role. Your customers are our own Ops, Product, Customer Success and Sales teams. Think of it as playing forward-deployed engineer for Alternative Payments itself: embedded with the teams that need you, understanding their real problems, and building the systems that solve them. Examples of what’s you’ll own:

  • Internal AI data infrastructure that consolidates what we know about our business and makes it usable across teams. Put AI at the center of how you work. We're an AI-forward team and expect you to build with it by default, leveraging it in your daily workflows as well as for team enablement, not just basic usage.

  • Building products we'd otherwise buy. We're replicating internal versions of Sales, CS, Marketing tools, built to fit exactly how we operate instead of bending our workflows to someone else's SaaS.

  • The dashboards that run the business. Our Ops dashboard, Finance dashboard, and the Super Admin dashboard, plus the automations behind them. This means understanding why something matters to the business, not just what needs to be built.

  • Own the work that starts as a prototype and has to become a real system: internal applications and automations, product integrations, features for new verticals, and agentic workflows hardened into deterministic ones.

  • Net-new product POCs. Working directly with the Product Engineering team on early-stage ideas before they become full initiatives, bringing business context and translating it into technical decisions.

  • Guardrails on AI-assisted development. Our BizOps team ships production code with AI assistance. You'll review that work (architecture, infrastructure decisions, PRs) to make sure it's safe, reliable, and doesn't quietly generate tech debt we have to unwind later.

  • Build for reliability, not just speed. Design and build systems with real attention to reliability, performance, and maintainability. This is software that moves real money, so the bar is production-grade from day one.

  • Plug into the engineering team through code review, architecture feedback, and shared standards, so what you ship is production-grade and you get sharper with every initiative.

You'll sit within Engineering but work alongside our Business Operations and Product Engineering teams. You will support our non-technical subject matter experts in deploying product to our production codebase, building systems from scratch and refining our coding harnesses to make them more use-friendly for non-technical users.

We run parallel initiatives in small, high-autonomy teams, and we expect the people who join us to step up, make decisions, and take accountability for outcomes, technical and otherwise.

What you'll bring

  • Deep architectural knowledge. You can look at a system and tell whether it's built right, not just whether it works.

  • Platform/infrastructure fluency. You understand what's underneath the application layer (Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, data pipelines) even if you're not deploying it every day.

  • Strong software engineering ability within a full-stack range. You ship production code independently and have owned real systems end to end. You move comfortably between frontend and backend.

  • An AI-native operating bias. AI is your default way of working: multiple models, custom agents, and specialized contexts integrated into how you plan, build, and ship, not just Copilot autocomplete.

  • Proficiency in, or the ability to quickly ramp on, our stack: TypeScript, Next.js, and Python for internal tooling, and Go or Rust, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, and AWS on the core platform.

  • Experience designing and evolving scalable systems, with a clear point of view on the tradeoffs involved for all stakeholders and end-users.

  • A demonstrated ability to take a project from end-to-end: technical execution, stakeholder communication, and delivery accountability.

  • Cross-functional instincts. You're comfortable moving between Operations, Product, and Data and switching context across very different stakeholders without losing the thread.

  • A bias toward business impact. You want to solve real operational problems and understand how the business actually runs and makes money.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, with the judgment to work autonomously, make decisions, and take accountability for outcomes.

  • Pragmatism and speed. You know when to build something fast and scrappy and when to make it bulletproof, and you can flex across domains without spreading yourself thin.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience at a fintech or payments company, or somewhere you worked close to how money moves.

  • Experience contributing to billing, payments, or quote-to-cash systems.

  • Experience building internal tools, admin panels, or business-facing dashboards.

  • Familiarity with event-driven architectures (RabbitMQ or similar).

  • Background at a fast-scaling startup, or anywhere you owned systems end-to-end close to the business.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary tailored to your experience, skills, and expertise.

  • The base compensation range for this role is $200,000 - 250,000, plus equity. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the approximate total target compensation for the position. Within the range, individual pay is determined by factors including relevant skills, experience, education/training.

  • Equity opportunities so you can share in our growth and success.

  • Unlimited PTO and flexibility when you need it the most.

  • Yearly learning & development stipend to help you grow and do your best work.

Why choose Alternative Payments?

At Alternative Payments, you'll do work that truly matters.

  • Own your impact: Build the internal systems the whole company runs on, and see your work used across the business every single day.

  • Collaborate: Work with a diverse, innovative team where every voice is heard and great ideas come from anywhere.

  • Grow with us: Your career journey is top of mind. We prioritize internal growth and give you the space to shape your path based on your goals, whether that's deepening your expertise in your domain or exploring something new.

  • Thrive in a supportive culture: As a scaling start-up, there's a lot to be done and initiative is key. We believe in shared learning, open communication, and building each other up. When one of us grows, we all do.

Want to see what we're actually building?

We made a short video so you don't have to take our word for it. Get a glimpse of our product, our people, and the problems we're solving, then decide if it sounds like your kind of place.

Our values

  • Transparency & Honesty: We communicate openly and truthfully with partners, investors, and each other so everyone understands where we stand and where we're headed.

  • Resourcefulness & AI: We stay scrappy, find creative solutions, and make progress even when the path isn't obvious. We have a bias for action and seek out the information and resources necessary to make decisions and move quickly.

  • Partnership: We win and lose together. We collaborate with our partners, investors, and teammates to tackle big challenges and reach shared goals.

  • Revolutionary & Boldness: We challenge conventions, take calculated risks, and build better, stronger solutions that move our business and the industry forward.

  • Accountability: We take ownership of our decisions and results. We follow through on our commitments knowing our work directly impacts our partners, our team and our business.

Applying to Alternative Payments

We're looking for candidates who are ready to step in and make an impact from day one. We know that sometimes people hold back unless they meet every requirement, but if you're excited about the role, bring relevant experience, and are ready to contribute, we want to hear from you!

All resumes are reviewed by our small but mighty talent team. While we may use AI tools to help prioritize applications, real people are behind every resume review and hiring decision. We're also committed to an inclusive and accessible process. If you require reasonable accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know upon being selected to interview.

jobs.excerpt: Community & Brand ManagerCompany: CyberNut Reports to: CEO and VP of Marketing Location: Los Angeles preferred (in-office; finding someone in LA is our ideal scenario).
jobs.description:
Community & Brand Manager

Company: CyberNut

Reports to: CEO and VP of Marketing

Location: Los Angeles preferred (in-office; finding someone in LA is our ideal scenario). Remote within the US considered.

Travel: Frequent travel across the country to customer sites, school districts, and K-12 conferences

Type: Full-time

About CyberNut

CyberNut is a fast-growing K-12 cybersecurity startup protecting more than 1 million students and staff across hundreds of school districts. Schools are one of the most targeted sectors for phishing and ransomware, and most security training was built for corporate boardrooms, not classrooms. We built CyberNut for schools.

Our platform trains teachers, staff, and students to spot phishing, scams, and account compromise as they happen, not once a year. Districts get automated, always-on phishing simulations themed to the tools schools actually use, one-click threat reporting right from the inbox, and short, gamified lessons that take minutes instead of hours. Our squirrel mascot, acorn rewards, and school leaderboards have turned security training into something staff and students actually talk about.

About the role

We are looking for a content creator who lives on social media and wants to build a brand people genuinely root for. You have native experience building, publishing, and creating content on TikTok, Instagram, and LinkedIn, and you know what makes people stop scrolling.

This is a boots-on-the-ground role at a fast-growing startup. You will travel around the country to meet our districts, show up at conferences, film content on site, and turn customer love into customer engagement. You will be part community builder, part brand ambassador, and the voice and face of CyberNut on social.

Why it exists: many of our districts like the brand as much as they use the platform. Leaderboards get posted, swag gets worn at conferences, and IT directors call themselves "a CyberNut school." Nobody on the team is accountable for growing that energy on purpose. This role owns it.

You will report directly to our CEO and our VP of Marketing, and work closely with Customer Success.

What you will own

Your time will split roughly across three areas: brand activation (about 35%), community and engagement (about 35%), and brand, social media, and content (about 30%). The split will flex by quarter.

1. Brand activation in every district

Buying CyberNut is not the same as being a CyberNut school. Activation is the work of making the brand visible, felt, and owned inside a district, and it looks different for a 2,000-student rural district than for a 40,000-student suburban one.

  • Build an activation plan for every new customer during onboarding, alongside their Customer Success Manager: who the champion is, where the brand will show up (staff kickoff, hallways, the IT newsletter, the board meeting), which program launches first, and what the district will be proud of in 90 days.

  • Track the activation level of every existing account (dormant, launched, visible, owned), review the lowest tier with Customer Success each month, and bring a plan to move each account up.

  • Create and ship the activation kit: launch decks for staff meetings, mascot and poster assets, leaderboard displays for IT offices and staff lounges, email templates for superintendents and principals, and swag for the first winners.

  • Run the launch moment. The first leaderboard reveal or the first trophy delivery should be an event, not an email.

  • Tailor the plan to each district. A single champion IT director needs a different plan than a district with a cabinet-level sponsor. The goal is the same: staff say "we're a CyberNut school" without being prompted.

2. Community and engagement

  • Run competitive leaderboard programs across customers: district vs. district, school vs. school, department vs. department. For example, a fall "Phish Bowl" where 25 districts compete on report rate for six weeks, with sponsored prizes and a trophy that travels.

  • Design and ship recurring promotions and events: Cybersecurity Awareness Month kits, end-of-year awards, a "first 90 days" challenge for new customers, and a winter swag drop for top performers.

  • Build and host customer community calls to learn which gamification loops drive the most excitement and engagement: a customer call where IT directors share what worked, and an online community space.

  • Partner with Customer Success on low-engagement accounts. When participation is flat, you bring the activation play (a leaderboard launch, a principal challenge, a superintendent shout-out) instead of another reminder email.

  • Make engagement visible outside the district. A school that climbs the leaderboard sees itself celebrated on CyberNut's channels the same week.

3. Brand ambassador, social media, and content

You own CyberNut's social channels. We want CyberNut showing up everywhere: TikTok, Instagram, and LinkedIn. What Duolingo did with its owl, we want you to help us do with our squirrel.

  • Own the company social accounts on TikTok, Instagram, and LinkedIn with a weekly content calendar you run. Marketing sets brand guidelines and campaign priorities; you create, film, and publish the day-to-day content, about 4 to 5 posts a week, most of them built from what customers are doing.

  • Bring the CyberNut squirrel to life as a personality people follow, with recurring formats, trends, and moments that make the mascot recognizable well beyond our customers.

  • Get on camera. Film on site at districts and conferences, try new formats, and do fun, creative things that push the brand forward.

  • Own the swag program end to end: what we make, who earns it, how it ships, and the budget. Think limited editions for top performers and referrers, not giveaways for everyone.

  • Show up at regional K-12 IT conferences and state ed-tech events with customers, not just a booth. For example, co-present with a customer IT director on how their district raised its report rate.

  • Run public customer recognition: a monthly "CyberNut School of the Month," social shout-outs for IT directors, and a wall of fame at our booth.

  • Turn every program into content. A six-week competition is six weeks of posts: launch, standings, a mid-point upset, final results, a winner interview, and the trophy delivery.

  • Make customers the stars. Tag districts and IT directors, invite them to share, and give champions an ambassador kit (templates, captions, photo guidelines) so they can post without waiting on you.

  • Treat social as an engagement channel: reply to comments, message champions, and celebrate a district's post within the hour.

How success is measured

This role is measured on outcomes, not activity. Success means more districts that are visibly and proudly engaged with CyberNut, a social presence that keeps growing, and that engagement showing up in higher report rates, stronger renewals, and more customer referrals. You will review leading indicators monthly (activation levels, program participation, report rates, social reach and engagement, and customer stories) with our CEO, VP of Marketing, and the Customer Success team.

How you will work with the team

  • Customer Success: you bring activation plans, kits, and plays for stuck accounts, plus early warning when a champion goes quiet. They share account health, renewal timing, and who the real champion is.

  • Sales: you surface warm referrals and reference customers. Sales owns every commercial conversation, including expansion. When a district wants to buy something, you introduce the owner and step back.

  • Marketing: you supply day-to-day social content, customer stories, case study leads, and conference co-presenters. Marketing provides brand guidelines, campaign priorities, swag design, and paid amplification of the best posts.

  • Product: you bring community feedback and pilot participants. Product provides early access and roadmap previews for champions.

What you bring

  • You are a TikTok and Instagram native and a natural content creator. You are not shy on camera and you are happy to do fun, creative things outside your comfort zone.

  • 2+ years in community management, customer marketing, brand, content creation, or social media, ideally at a B2B or education technology company.

  • A track record of running programs, events, or campaigns that measurably increased engagement, brand awareness, and activation.

  • Strong writing and an eye for visual content. You can turn a customer win into a post people want to share.

  • Comfort owning company social accounts on TikTok, Instagram, and LinkedIn, plus a content calendar.

  • Excitement about frequent travel and the energy and judgment to represent CyberNut in person at conferences and customer events.

  • Strong organization: you can run many districts, programs, and deadlines at once without dropping the details.

  • Bonus: experience in K-12 education, with school IT teams, or in cybersecurity.

Why CyberNut

Hundreds of school districts already trust CyberNut to protect their staff and students. You will build the community and the social brand around CyberNut from the ground up, work directly with our CEO and VP of Marketing, and see your work show up in how districts talk about us.

jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a fully remote position and we're considering candidates in Spain.

About Product Management

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own the experience for your product as well as its roadmap and competitive positioning, and you will collaborate with company leadership on setting your product's goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.

Product Managers are the bridge that connects R&D to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

The role

As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you'll own the Grafana Labs offerings that run outside our standard multi-tenant SaaS. That includes Grafana Federal Cloud, for organizations that need FedRAMP-authorized observability: US federal agencies; state, local, and education (SLED) customers; and commercial companies that sell FedRAMP offerings of their own. It also includes Grafana Cloud Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC), which delivers the full Grafana Cloud experience while the customer pays the infrastructure bill directly to their cloud provider, saving them significantly at scale.

Your mission is to make Grafana Labs the obvious choice for organizations that can't use standard SaaS because of compliance, data, or cost-at-scale constraints. Deployment choices change the product: features that are simple in standard SaaS can be hard, expensive, or impossible in a regulated or customer-owned environment. You’ll be responsible for adapting existing Grafana Cloud capabilities to these environments, deciding which features come in, which wait, and which stay out, and occasionally building something specific to BYOC or Federal Cloud. You'll also help shape which deployment models we offer next.

Along the way, you’ll use AI tools daily to speed up research, analyze product signals, and develop positioning, applying strong judgment to the results.

As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you will:

  • Define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Grafana Bring Your Own Cloud and Grafana Federal Cloud products, using product data and market research to balance customer value against engineering cost and technical constraints
  • Own positioning, messaging, and differentiation for these products, including how they compare to regular Grafana Cloud, and partner with Product Marketing on launches, competitive analysis, enablement, and demand programs
  • Partner with Engineering and Technical Program Management on buildouts for these environments, balancing customer timelines with engineering capacity
  • Work directly with customers, prospects, and the field on strategic deals and brief partners, resellers, and analysts on our deployment options
  • Partner with Security, Compliance, and Legal to work through product changes affecting our authorization or existing customer commitments

We’re excited about you because you have

  • 5+ years of product management experience on a technical B2B product, or a technical background (software engineering, solutions architecture, SRE, or technical program management) plus a demonstrated move into product ownership
  • Hands-on experience with a non-standard SaaS deployment model, such as self-managed, air-gapped, sovereign, BYOC, single-tenant, or FedRAMP/government cloud, and a firsthand understanding of how it changes the product, its operations, and its economics
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure, platform software, or developer tools
  • Clear product and go-to-market judgment: you've shaped what a product should be and how it's positioned and sold, not only when it ships
  • Interest in working with US public sector customers and learning their needs and buying cycles. Deep compliance expertise isn't required.
  • Experience leading across multiple teams without direct authority, with excellent written and verbal communication in a remote, globally distributed organization

Bonus Points

  • Experience selling to or building for US federal, state, or local government customers, or other highly regulated industries
  • Familiarity with government or sovereign cloud frameworks, such as FedRAMP, StateRAMP/GovRAMP, BSI C5, or SecNumCloud, or with offerings such as AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, AWS European Sovereign Cloud, or GCP Sovereign Cloud
  • Experience with pricing and packaging across deployment models
  • Experience with observability, monitoring, or other data-intensive infrastructure products
  • Experience working with resellers, systems integrators, or cloud marketplace partners
  • Familiarity with open source software or commercial open source companies

In Spain, the base compensation range for this role is EUR 106,680 - EUR 128,016. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

Equal Opportunity Employer:Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow.

jobs.excerpt: About DoitWe are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more.
jobs.description:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Engineer to take technical ownership of complex products and systems and raise the engineering bar across the team.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review code, solve difficult engineering problems, guide other engineers and drive major initiatives from idea to production.

You should be comfortable moving between architecture and implementation — making strong technical decisions while still being close enough to the code to execute when needed.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the technical design and execution of major products, features and engineering initiatives.

  • Design scalable, reliable and maintainable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Stay hands-on with engineering through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Make architecture decisions and technical trade-offs that balance speed, scalability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Break ambiguous product and technical problems into clear engineering solutions and execution plans.

  • Set a high bar for code quality, system design, testing, security, observability and production reliability.

  • Review technical designs and code from other engineers and provide clear, actionable feedback.

  • Mentor engineers and help strengthen technical capability across the team.

  • Identify technical risks, bottlenecks and architectural weaknesses before they become larger problems.

  • Work closely with engineering, product, design and AI teams to ship high-quality products quickly.

  • Improve engineering tooling, development practices and automation to increase team velocity.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills with experience making technical decisions for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Proven experience leading major engineering projects or providing technical leadership to other engineers.

  • Comfortable reviewing code, debugging complex issues and working directly with production systems.

  • Able to explain complex technical decisions clearly and influence engineers across teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity and take ownership from problem definition through production.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to simplify and when deeper engineering investment is required.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who want a leadership title but no longer want to write or review code.

  • People who only want to work within one narrow technical area.

  • Engineers who wait for complete specifications before starting.

  • Candidates who over-engineer solutions when a simpler approach would achieve the outcome.

  • Engineers who focus only on implementation without understanding the product or business problem.

  • People who avoid production incidents, difficult debugging or ownership after release.

  • Candidates who make vague claims about technical leadership without being able to explain what they personally designed, built, shipped or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for technical leaders with real engineering career highlights.

A strong highlight is not simply having a senior title or working at a famous technology company. A strong highlight means you personally designed, built, shipped or scaled a serious product, platform or system and can go deep into the technical decisions behind it.

You should be able to demonstrate both technical depth and technical leadership — someone who can solve difficult engineering problems personally while making the engineers around them stronger.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) is the executive responsible for protecting the organization's information, technology infrastructure, applications, data, and digital services from cyber threats and security risks.

Within Insurance & Investments, the CISO leads enterprise cybersecurity, information security governance, cyber risk management, security architecture, incident response, regulatory compliance, identity and access management, third-party security, and business continuity/cyber resilience.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and execute the enterprise cybersecurity and information security strategy.

Establish information security policies, standards, controls, and governance frameworks.

Lead enterprise-wide cybersecurity risk management.

Protect sensitive customer, financial, investment, policyholder, employee, and corporate data.

Security Operations (SOC)

Threat Detection & Response

Incident Response

Security Architecture

Vulnerability Management

Penetration Testing

Identity & Access Management

Endpoint Security

Network Security

Cloud Security

Application Security

Data Security

Establish and manage cyber incident response and crisis-management processes.

Develop and test Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery, and Cyber Resilience plans.

Establish cybersecurity KPIs, KRIs, dashboards, and executive reporting.

Manage cybersecurity budgets, vendors, managed security providers, and strategic technology partners.

Lead and develop information-security and cybersecurity teams.

jobs.excerpt: Sprinto is an Autonomous Trust Platform that centralizes trust requirements across security frameworks, vendors, and customers.
jobs.description:
Sprinto is an Autonomous Trust Platform that centralizes trust requirements across security frameworks, vendors, and customers.

Sprinto autonomously executes tasks needed to maintain trust across compliance, audits, risk management, vendor risk, privacy, and AI governance, enabling organizations to maintain a strong, reliable trust posture without draining operational bandwidth and resources on repetitive tasks.

Backed by top-tier investors such as Accel, Elevation, and Blume Ventures, we’ve raised$31.8M in funding to fuel our mission. Trusted by over 4,000 organizations across 75 countries, Sprinto helps organizations stay audit-ready, manage real-time risks, and scale fearlessly. With 300+ native integrations and AI-driven automation, Sprinto supports 200+ global security standards natively, including SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and more. Sprinto's extensible architecture enables organizations to build and support an infinite number of custom integrations and frameworks.

Founded in 2020 by second-time founders Girish Redekar and Raghuveer Kancherla, Sprinto powers compliance for organizations like Whatfix, Encora, Anaconda, Whatnot, Ultrahuman, WeWork, Everstage, AI Foundation, HackerRank, and many more.

Life as a Sprinter -

Nobody succeeds at Sprinto by staying in their lane.

We are organized around problems, not job titles. Sprinters take ownership beyond their role, solve hard problems, and care deeply about the impact they create. If something can be improved, fixed, or built, we don't wait for permission; we step in.

Being remote means we rely less on proximity and more on trust. We write things down, communicate openly, and move quickly because great teams aren't built by sitting together, they're built by pulling in the same direction.

We believe progress beats perfection, feedback is a gift, and doing the right thing matters, even when nobody is watching.

And while we move with urgency, we never move alone.

The mission -

Some of our most valuable customer conversations begin in a room: a CISO dinner, a founder meetup, a practitioner roundtable. Your mission is to turn those conversations into a predictable, growing source of pipeline for Sprinto.

You’ll own our global field marketing strategy across the US, EMEA, and APAC, reaching startup and SMB founders as well as mid-market security, GRC, and IT leaders. You’ll decide where we show up, whom we bring together, and where every field dollar goes.

Where you'll leave your mark?

    Reporting to the Head of Marketing, you’ll sit on the Marketing leadership team and lead three regional field marketers covering US Mid-Market, APAC/EMEA Mid-Market, and Startup/SMB programs. You’ll also own GRC Hub and Secure Circle, our CISO peer group, and bring field programs into our broader ABM motion.

    This is a player-coach role. You’ll build the strategy, systems, and team while staying close to execution, whether that means hosting an executive dinner, testing a new market, or working with Sales on an account-specific experience.

    • Own the global field strategy and pipeline. Build annual and quarterly plans across the US, EMEA, and APAC, aligned with regional sales priorities. Own sourced and influenced pipeline, budgets, and ROI, using program reviews within 30 days to decide what to scale, improve, or stop.

    • Build programs that move buyers forward. Run conferences, executive dinners, roundtables, and partner-led experiences. Align with Sales and SDRs on target accounts, meeting goals, outreach, follow-up, and nurture, and embed account-specific field plays into our ABM motion.

    • Grow communities and executive relationships. Own GRC Hub and Secure Circle, creating programming that builds membership, engagement, and pipeline. Bring the right buyers into the room and turn members into speakers, hosts, and advocates.

    • Lead the team and build repeatable systems. Coach three regional field marketers, own hiring and headcount planning, and build reusable playbooks for execution and reporting. Manage vendors and agencies, and partner with Product Marketing, Marketing Operations, and Finance to keep programs consistent and well-run.

    • Experiment and turn learning into action. Test new markets, formats, gifting, and activations with clear hypotheses and budget caps. Use AI to improve research, targeting, content, and reporting, and turn successful experiments into programs the team can repeat.

The kind of builder we're looking for -

    • You’ve built and led field marketing teams. You bring 8–12 years in B2B marketing, including 5+ in SaaS field or regional marketing and 3+ managing field marketers, ideally across regions.

    • You can connect programs to commercial outcomes. You’ve owned multi-region budgets and pipeline targets, can demonstrate program ROI, and are comfortable building your own analysis in HubSpot.

    • You understand different markets and buyers. You’ve run programs in at least two of the US, UK/Europe, Middle East, or India/APAC, reaching startup/SMB buyers and mid-market or enterprise security, IT, or GRC leaders.

    • You bring people together around execution. You build strong partnerships with Sales, SDRs, and Partners, and are equally comfortable hosting senior executives, presenting to leadership, and getting into event details.

    • You build, learn, and adapt. You move quickly through ambiguity, use evidence to prioritise, and turn lessons into practical playbooks. You stay close to execution while helping your team grow.

      • You’ll bring additional perspective if you’ve worked in cybersecurity, compliance, or GRC; built a practitioner community or executive peer group; designed account-level field programs; or helped a Series B+ company turn founder-led initiatives into a repeatable field motion.

      If you’ve built field programs that created meaningful buyer relationships, measurable pipeline, and a stronger playbook for the next round, we’d love to hear how you did it.

How we care for our Sprinters?

  • Work wherever you are: We are 100% remote, so you get to choose if you want to work from home, a cafe, the hills, or the beach.
  • Co-working, on the house: If co-working is your jam, we offer a generous annual allowance.
  • We care about your learning: We are invested in seeing you grow and commit USD 1,000 annually to help you level up your skills.
  • We count your spark, not your leaves: Unlimited leave so you can reset when you need to.
  • Your Safety Net, Woven In: Health insurance with coverage up to INR 10 lakh for you and your family, accident protection of an additional INR 10 lakh, and life insurance worth 3x your annual salary.
  • Workspace setup of your dreams: We chip in INR 35,000 to help you build a setup that works for you.


Inclusion & Diversity -

At Sprinto, talent, curiosity, and ownership matter more than where you come from. We hire people for the problems they can solve, the impact they create, and the way they help others succeed—not their background, identity, or personal circumstances. We believe the best teams are built when people with different perspectives come together around a shared ambition to build something meaningful.

We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a fair, inclusive, and accessible hiring process for everyone.

About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Engineer to take technical ownership of complex products and systems and raise the engineering bar across the team.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review code, solve difficult engineering problems, guide other engineers and drive major initiatives from idea to production.

You should be comfortable moving between architecture and implementation — making strong technical decisions while still being close enough to the code to execute when needed.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the technical design and execution of major products, features and engineering initiatives.

  • Design scalable, reliable and maintainable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Stay hands-on with engineering through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Make architecture decisions and technical trade-offs that balance speed, scalability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Break ambiguous product and technical problems into clear engineering solutions and execution plans.

  • Set a high bar for code quality, system design, testing, security, observability and production reliability.

  • Review technical designs and code from other engineers and provide clear, actionable feedback.

  • Mentor engineers and help strengthen technical capability across the team.

  • Identify technical risks, bottlenecks and architectural weaknesses before they become larger problems.

  • Work closely with engineering, product, design and AI teams to ship high-quality products quickly.

  • Improve engineering tooling, development practices and automation to increase team velocity.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills with experience making technical decisions for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Proven experience leading major engineering projects or providing technical leadership to other engineers.

  • Comfortable reviewing code, debugging complex issues and working directly with production systems.

  • Able to explain complex technical decisions clearly and influence engineers across teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity and take ownership from problem definition through production.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to simplify and when deeper engineering investment is required.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who want a leadership title but no longer want to write or review code.

  • People who only want to work within one narrow technical area.

  • Engineers who wait for complete specifications before starting.

  • Candidates who over-engineer solutions when a simpler approach would achieve the outcome.

  • Engineers who focus only on implementation without understanding the product or business problem.

  • People who avoid production incidents, difficult debugging or ownership after release.

  • Candidates who make vague claims about technical leadership without being able to explain what they personally designed, built, shipped or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for technical leaders with real engineering career highlights.

A strong highlight is not simply having a senior title or working at a famous technology company. A strong highlight means you personally designed, built, shipped or scaled a serious product, platform or system and can go deep into the technical decisions behind it.

You should be able to demonstrate both technical depth and technical leadership — someone who can solve difficult engineering problems personally while making the engineers around them stronger.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

About the role

The Workforce Analyst provides the analytical foundation for effective resource planning and execution across the Rapid Data Center Deployment (RDD) organization. Reporting to the Workforce Manager, this role is responsible for converting complex project schedules, contractor inputs, and timekeeping data into actionable workforce insights. Unlike account-dedicated management roles, the Workforce Analyst operates across single or multiple program accounts as needed, ensuring consistent operational visibility, demand modeling, and labor tracking. The ideal candidate is highly analytical, detail-oriented, and operationally focused, with the ability to translate project schedules, resource plans, partner staffing inputs, and timekeeping data into actionable workforce insights. This individual must be comfortable working across PMO, Workforce Management, onsite resource leads, partner teams, Finance, Professional Services, and other stakeholders to identify workforce gaps, validate labor information, escalate staffing risks, and improve workforce tracking discipline.

Location: Saline, MI

What you'll be doing

Workforce Planning, Tracking & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate workforce trackers, dashboards, and reporting standards covering utilization, attendance, readiness, and contractor labor metrics.
  • Collaborate with PMO, WFM, and project leads to aggregate schedules, skill needs, and deployment timelines into a forward-looking capacity model.
  • Monitor scheduled versus actual staffing across internal and contractor teams, surfacing coverage gaps, attendance trends, and resource risks.
  • Validate labor hours, travel premiums, per diems, and contractor timecards to support accurate AP reconciliation, invoice dispute resolution, and cost tracking.
  • Identify and document operational bottlenecks—including staffing shortfalls, badging delays, and timekeeping errors—escalating root causes for swift resolution.
  • Lead routine WFM operational reviews, presenting key metrics, root-cause analyses, and action plans to account leadership.
  • Track third-party labor availability, site access readiness, onboarding status, and replacements to ensure uninterrupted deployment continuity.

Process Improvement & Stakeholder Partnership

  • Continuously refine WFM reporting, timekeeping reconciliation, and capacity forecasting tools to streamline data workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve forecast accuracy.
  • Serve as the primary workforce data contact across PMO, WFM, Finance, site leads, and external partners, delivering actionable insights on labor utilization, coverage gaps, and deployment readiness.
  • Champion company core values and strategic priorities through operational rigor, continuous improvement, and cross-functional collaboration.

What you have

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in workforce management, resource management, workforce analytics, labor planning, project controls, operations analysis, contractor workforce coordination, or a related resource-management role.
  • Proven ability to balance analytical support across multiple accounts, large-scale resource pools, including 24x7 operations and workforces of more than 1,000 employees, contractors, or partner-supplied resources while prioritizing deliverables in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong proficiency in Excel, data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau), and WFM or ERP resource planning systems.
  • Keen eye for reconciling disparate data sources (timecards, project plans, contractor logs) into accurate, executive-ready reporting.
  • Legally eligible to work in the United States.

What you can expect

There’s so much more to enjoy about being at Computacenter than just having a rewarding career. In addition to offering competitive compensation plans and long-term career opportunities, we provide an attractive mix of benefit plans to contribute to your good health, future financial security, and peace of mind.

About us

Computacenter is a leading independent technology partner, trusted by large corporate and public sector organizations. We help our world-renowned customers to source, transform, and manage their IT infrastructure to deliver digital transformation, enabling users and their business. We’re a public company quoted on the London FTSE 250 (CCC.L) and employ over 21,000 people worldwide. In the US, we support some of the country’s best-known businesses with regional hubs in San Francisco and Irvine, CA; Norcross, GA; Plano, TX; and New York City; and Integration Centers in Silicon Valley and Atlanta.

About Carewell

Are you an impact-driven problem solver who is passionate about making a difference in the lives of others while contributing to a fast growing start-up? Join Carewell and be a part of a team that creates impactful solutions for caregivers and their unique challenges. We're looking for hardworking individuals committed to raising the bar and striving for impact, scalability, and simplicity. Build your career with Carewell, a category-defining business dedicated to making caregiving easier.

Our Data Philosophy

We build for leverage, not volume. That means self-service by default — stakeholders should be able to answer their own questions, with us as partners on the analysis that actually requires one. It means building everything so it can be used by LLMs, not just people; AI tooling isn't perfect, but we'd rather work at its edge than wait for it to be easy. And it means impact above all: we prioritize work with a measurable effect on the business, and we say no to work that doesn't move it forward.

About the Role

Carewell runs on a mix of e-commerce fundamentals and service delivery — merchandising, marketing, and revenue on one side; Care Services and customer support on the other. As the Business Insights Analyst, your role exists to make sure every part of that business can see, in numbers, whether it's working.

You won't be reporting the news. You'll be figuring out what's actually driving the number to move, building the report or tracker that lets a stakeholder self-monitor going forward, and helping them land on the levers worth pulling next. You'll work across financial reporting, marketing efficiency, merchandising and margin, customer cohort behavior, and Care Services productivity — not as a subject matter expert in any one of them, but as someone who's demonstrated, repeatedly, that they can get fluent in a new part of a business fast enough to build something useful in it.

This role reports to the Sr. Director of Analytics & Data Engineering, who owns the canonical data model and BI architecture. You won't own that architecture — but you'll work inside it daily, and you'll need to understand table structure well enough to direct how existing tables should be re-engineered to support the analysis you're building.

This is a role built for someone who wants to go deep on the analysis and the business itself, not climb toward people management. We're looking for 3–5 years of experience and someone who's genuinely excited about spending the next several years getting better at this craft, not treating it as a one-year stepping stone.

What You’ll Do

Build Reports That Drive Action, Not Just Reporting

  • Design and build reports and dashboards that help stakeholders self-monitor their part of the business
  • Go beyond "what happened" to "what's driving it" — identify the underlying business drivers behind metric movement
  • Partner with stakeholders to use data to drive strategic business decisions
  • Help identify the KPIs a given team or function should actually be watching, and build the reporting that tracks them on an ongoing basis
  • Build and maintain monthly financial reports, incorporating light financial analysis across revenue, margin, and cost lines
  • Retire or simplify reports that no longer drive decisions, so stakeholders aren't left sorting signal from noise

Work Across the Business

  • Marketing efficiency analysis: CAC, LTV, spend efficiency, channel-level performance
  • Merchandising, revenue, and profit/margin analysis: product- and category-level performance, margin drivers
  • Customer cohort behavior: retention curves, repeat purchase patterns, Autoship performance
  • Care Services productivity analysis: throughput, service-level metrics, staffing efficiency
  • No single one of these needs to be a specialty coming in — you'll need to show you can ramp into a new analytical domain and produce something useful, not just competent, in it

Turn Feedback Into Measurable Levers

  • Take stakeholder input — a hunch, a complaint, an open question — and turn it into a concrete, testable hypothesis about what lever to pull
  • Build the tracking needed to measure results once that lever is pulled, before the lever is pulled, not after
  • Close the loop — report back on whether the lever worked, and adjust the tracking or the hypothesis if it didn't
  • Flag when a stakeholder's request points to a bigger underlying question worth raising, rather than just answering exactly what was asked

Communicate Across the Organization

  • Work directly with stakeholders at every level, from individual contributors to senior leadership
  • Strong, clear written and verbal communication is required; polished presentation skills are not
  • Translate technical or data-heavy findings into plain language a non-analytical stakeholder can act on

Work With the Data Foundation (Not Own It)

  • Understand table structure and data model design well enough to give clear direction on how existing tables should be re-engineered to support your analysis
  • Write complex, efficient SQL to build and maintain your own analytical queries independently
  • Use AI tools (Claude, Claude Code, Claude Cowork) and Hex as part of your everyday workflow — from day one, not as a learning curve
  • Escalate data model or table-structure issues to rather than working around them repeatedly

Outcomes You’ll Drive

  • Actionable, Not Just Accurate: Reports and dashboards that lead stakeholders to a decision or a lever to pull, not just a status update
  • Trusted Monthly Financials: Monthly financial reporting that's accurate, timely, and consistent enough for leadership to rely on without re-checking it
  • KPIs That Stick: Self-monitoring metrics and dashboards that teams actually keep using — not built once and abandoned
  • Levers Tracked to Results: A clear record of levers identified from stakeholder input, with tracking in place to show whether each one worked
  • Cross-Functional Fluency: Demonstrated ability to ramp into a new part of the business (Marketing, Merchandising, Finance, Care Services) and produce useful analysis within it, without requiring deep subject-matter ramp-up time
  • Day-One AI Leverage: Visible, practical use of AI tools in the analytical workflow from the start — faster turnaround and broader coverage than a comparable analyst working without them

What You’ll Bring

  • 3–5 years of experience in analytics, business intelligence, reporting, or a closely related analytical role
  • Demonstrated experience working across multiple functional areas of a business (i.e. marketing, product, finance, operations)
  • Strong SQL skills — comfortable writing complex analytical queries independently, including joins across multiple tables and aggregations at different levels of grain
  • Working understanding of relational table structure and data modeling concepts — able to read an existing schema and identify where it should change to support new analysis
  • Proven experience with modern reporting tools (Hex, Looker, Omni, Etc.)
  • Practical, hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or similar) to accelerate analytical work — able to apply this productively from day one, not as something to be trained on
  • E-commerce or DTC experience strongly preferred; service-business experience (support, care, or operations) also valuable given Carewell's Care Services function
  • A specific example, from a past role, of a report or metric you built that changed a stakeholder's decision — not just informed it
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfort presenting findings to stakeholders at all levels
  • A track record that suggests genuine interest in going deep on analytical craft over the next several years, rather than using this as a fast step toward a management track
  • Degree in a quantitative, business, or related field preferred

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation
  • Health, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • Short-term Disability and Life Insurance (100% employer-sponsored)
  • Long-term Disability
  • Supplemental Life Insurance (employee-sponsored)
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan
  • 100% Remote
  • Generous paid time off and 6 paid holidays
  • Employee discount

Learn more about the Carewell story.

Carewell is a category-defining business that is dedicated to providing the most trusted and reputable retail source for caregiving products. Our vast selection of expert-vetted products includes incontinence supplies, wound care, nutrition, mobility aids, and more, all available at the best prices with fast, reliable shipping. We are proud to have been recognized as one of the fastest-growing companies in the US, ranked on the Inc. 5000, and named one of the most customer-centric companies in the world by Forbes in 2022. At Carewell, we understand the importance of caregiving, and we strive to provide the highest quality products to help caregivers provide the best care possible for their loved ones.

As the number of older adults in the US grows, the need for caregiving solutions will only increase. By joining Carewell, you will have the opportunity to work in a space that is constantly evolving, with new challenges and opportunities for growth. We are committed to being architects of our own success, always striving to improve our teams, partnerships, and solutions to ensure impact, scalability, and simplicity. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to collaborate with like-minded individuals, using customer insights, data, research, and feedback to make decisions and create the most effective solutions. jobs.description:
Photonics Layout Engineer (Remote)

About us:

Voyant Photonics is bushing the boundaries of silicon photonic chips that steer and switch light at high speed. They power next generation, chip-scale FMCW LiDAR for robotics and autonomy, and optical circuit switches (OCS) for AI data centers. Based in NYC, we’re a hands-on team designing, building, and deploying frontier hardware to solve problems that matter, from how machines see to how AI scales.

Why Join Us?

At Voyant, you'll help develop some of the most sophisticated silicon photonic chips, spanning two applications: optical circuit switching for AI data centers and chip-scale LiDAR sensing.

You'll tackle challenging problems in large-scale photonic integration, including dense waveguide routing, multilayer photonic layouts, and complex die- and reticle-level floorplanning. Our PICs integrate hundreds to thousands of optical components, requiring innovative layout approaches that balance optical performance, chip dimensions, and manufacturability.

As a Photonic Layout Engineer, you'll take ownership of PIC layouts from initial floorplanning through tapeout. You'll have the opportunity to develop automated layout methodologies, solve complex routing challenges, and work closely with photonic designers and other engineering teams in a fast-paced startup environment.

What You'll Do:

  • Develop and implement layouts for complex photonic integrated circuits, from component-level test structures to large-scale system PICs.

  • Translate photonic schematics and design requirements into efficient, manufacturable GDSII layouts.

  • Implement dense waveguide routing, multilayer optical interconnects, and die- and reticle-level floorplanning.

  • Develop and maintain parameterized photonic component cells (PCells) and reusable layout libraries.

  • Create Python-based scripts and automation tools for layout generation, routing, and design verification.

  • Integrate photonic and electrical layouts, including electrical routing, contact pads, and packaging interfaces.

  • Perform and debug physical verification, including DRC, LVS, and optical connectivity checks.

  • Collaborate with photonic designers, packaging engineers, and foundry partners to optimize layouts and support tapeout submissions.

What We're Looking For

  • B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Photonics, Physics, Optical Engineering, or a related field.

  • 2+ years of experience in photonic integrated circuit layout, preferably in silicon photonics or a similar platform.

  • Proficiency with photonic layout tools such as GDSFactory, IPKISS, KLayout, or equivalent.

  • Strong Python scripting skills, including experience with layout automation or parameterized designs.

  • Experience with photonic waveguide routing, component placement, and chip-level layout integration.

  • Familiarity with silicon photonics foundry PDKs, design rules, and tapeout processes.

  • Strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and ability to collaborate in a multidisciplinary team.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with large-scale PIC layout, optical switching networks, or complex photonic routing architectures.

  • Experience with multilayer silicon/silicon nitride photonic platforms and interlayer optical transitions.

  • Experience developing automated routing, placement optimization, or layout generation algorithms.

  • Familiarity with Cadence Virtuoso, SKILL, or electrical layout and EDA integration.

Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Engineer to take technical ownership of complex products and systems and raise the engineering bar across the team.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review code, solve difficult engineering problems, guide other engineers and drive major initiatives from idea to production.

You should be comfortable moving between architecture and implementation — making strong technical decisions while still being close enough to the code to execute when needed.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the technical design and execution of major products, features and engineering initiatives.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.
