£competitive with fantastic bonuses, company car or car allowance & home-based contract & excellent company benefits

An exciting opportunity has now arisen for a Sales Specialist to join the Fresh Specialist team.

We're looking for a driven sales professional who thrives on winning new business, growing customer spend and building strong relationships. Working closely with Area Sales Managers, Business Development Managers and Sales Consultants, you'll help deliver volume, sales and margin growth across the region.

You'll maximise opportunities across both new and existing customers, helping teams identify growth opportunities and increase share of wallet. A key focus of the role will be supporting growth within our Meat & Poultry category, acting as a specialist resource and subject matter expert.

This role is remote based, but you must be within a commuting distance of the Region.

What you'll be doing:

  • To help increase volume, sales turnover and margin within Chilled & Frozen Meat & Poultry category by working closely with independent sales teams on all customer opportunities
  • To build excellent working relationships with customers, presenting & demonstrating the Meat & Poultry range accurately and professionally to help build trust and gain credibility
  • To promote the Brakes chilled meat & poultry proposition
  • Working closely with Area Sales Managers, Business Development Managers and dedicated telesales specialists to gain and develop new business & SOW
  • Work closely with dedicated telesales to help sell through products at risk & reduce waste, plus assist with any product questions/knowledge/advice
  • Actively participate and contribute to team meetings, training and developing knowledge within Brakes sales teams to maximise opportunities across their customer base
  • Accurate completion of weekly & monthly administration
  • Building and maintaining a robust pipeline, ensuring all details are captured through Salesforce
  • Maximise selling opportunities through analysis of customer requirements and gap-fill opportunities
  • Continually maintain competitor and market awareness
  • Jointly own and manage your personal and career development with your line manager

About you:

You'll be a confident relationship builder with proven sales, account management or business development experience. Commercially focused and target driven, you'll have a track record of identifying opportunities, influencing customers and delivering results.

The ideal candidate will have experience within the Meat & Poultry category, alongside a proven track record in sales, account management or business development. Experience within foodservice, fresh food or FMCG is highly desirable, coupled with the drive and determination to grow sales and win new business.

Ideally you'll have experience of:

  • Field sales, account management or business development
  • CRM system usage
  • Data analysis and reporting
  • KPI and target management
  • Customer relationship management

At Brakes everyone is welcome. We don’t want you to ‘fit our culture’ we want you to help define it and we actively celebrate the unique talents of each and every colleague. We don’t just look at your CV, we’re more focused on who you are and your potential. As part of our values, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone has a voice, is appreciated and has the same opportunities. We work hard to ensure that everyone feels part of our business, as we care for one another and connect the world through food and trusted partnerships. Our ultimate goal is to ensure that everyone belongs and thrives at Brakes and we recognise that Brakes can only thrive when everyone feels they belong. We'll do everything we can to support you during your application. If you need us to make any adjustments to our recruitment process, speak to our resourcing team who will be happy to support you.

Brakes

Built on a passion for food and feeding the nation, we are the UK’s largest foodservice supplier. Every day Brakes deliver the highest quality fresh and frozen food and ingredients from our nationwide network of distribution centres to some of the nation’s most famous pubs and restaurants, as well as schools, caterers, care homes and hospitals. Our customers depend on us, and our 8,000-strong workforce is dedicated and proud to be part of this vital provision. And we’re growing!

jobs.excerpt: we make the world better with dataDie Woodmark Consulting GmbH gehört zu den führenden deutschen IT-Beratungsunternehmen für AI, Data & Analytics.
jobs.description:
we make the world better with data

Die Woodmark Consulting GmbH gehört zu den führenden deutschen IT-Beratungsunternehmen für AI, Data & Analytics. Wir begeistern Menschen durch unsere Leidenschaft für Daten & Innovation. Das Leben unserer Werte Respekt, Offenheit, Vertrauen und Fürsorge sorgt für eine ausgezeichnete Unternehmenskultur und ist die Basis unseres Erfolgs.

Nutze auch du deine Leidenschaft für Daten & Innovation und erschließe mit uns deren Potenzial. So schaffen wir gemeinsam einen Mehrwert für Kunden, Gesellschaft und Umwelt.

deine bunte aufgabenpalette

Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit deinem Team moderne AI-Lösungen für unsere Kunden – von der ersten Anforderung über die Cloud-Architektur bis zum produktiven Einsatz. Dein Schwerpunkt liegt auf Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs) und agentenbasierten Anwendungen. Dabei verbindest du technisches Architekturverständnis mit praktischer Softwareentwicklung und setzt Lösungen vor allem auf AWS, aber auch auf Azure um.

Anforderungen verstehen und Lösungen gestalten: Gemeinsam mit unseren Kunden und Fachbereichen analysierst du Anforderungen, identifizierst geeignete AI-Anwendungsfälle und übersetzt diese in konkrete technische Lösungskonzepte. Du bewertest die Machbarkeit, wählst passende Technologien aus und entwickelst skalierbare, sichere und wirtschaftliche Cloud-Architekturen.

AI-Lösungen entwickeln und integrieren: Du entwickelst AI-Anwendungen auf Basis moderner Foundation Models und Cloud-Services wie Amazon Bedrock. Dabei setzt du unter anderem Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI Agents und Tool Calling ein. Du integrierst AI-Funktionalitäten über APIs und Schnittstellen in bestehende Unternehmenssysteme und sorgst dafür, dass benötigte Daten sicher und zuverlässig bereitgestellt werden. Bei komplexeren Datenanforderungen arbeitest du eng mit unseren Data-Engineering-Spezialisten zusammen.

Cloud Engineering und DevOps leben: Du setzt deine Architekturkonzepte auch selbst in Code um. Mit Python, Infrastructure as Code und modernen DevOps-Praktiken entwickelst du automatisierte, reproduzierbare und wartbare Lösungen. Dabei berücksichtigst du von Anfang an Anforderungen an Security, Performance, Monitoring, Skalierbarkeit und Kosten.

Verantwortung übernehmen: Du übernimmst die technische Verantwortung für kleinere Projekte oder Teilprojekte und begleitest AI-Lösungen von der Konzeption bis zum produktiven Betrieb. Du triffst fundierte Architektur- und Technologieentscheidungen, hinterfragst bestehende Ansätze und unterstützt weniger erfahrene Teammitglieder als technischer Sparringspartner.

Kommunikation ist das Maß aller Dinge: Du bist stets im intensiven Austausch mit

  • den Fachbereichen und Architekten für projektbezogene Abstimmungen
  • deinen Kunden, um Architekturentscheidungen transparent zu machen und Erwartungsmanagement sicherzustellen
  • deinem Projektteam, um technische Exzellenz und Projekterfolg zu gewährleisten
  • dem Woodmark Team, um Wissen zu AI-Architekturen, Cloud-Patterns und Best Practices zu teilen

das hast du auf lager

Projekterfahrung: Du hast mindestens 3 Jahre praktische Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung oder im Cloud Engineering und idealerweise bereits AI-Anwendungen in Kundenprojekten konzipiert und umgesetzt. Du verstehst das Zusammenspiel von Anwendungen, Daten, Cloud-Infrastruktur und AI-Services und kannst daraus eigenständig technische Lösungen entwickeln.

Expertise ist selbstverständlich: Du verfügst über

  • Sehr gute Kenntnisse in Python und Erfahrung in der Entwicklung professioneller Softwareanwendungen
  • Fundierte praktische Erfahrung mit AWS und dem Entwurf sowie der Umsetzung von Cloud-Architekturen
  • Erfahrung mit Generative AI, Large Language Models und der Integration von Foundation Models in Anwendungen, idealerweise mit Amazon Bedrock
  • Kenntnisse moderner AI-Architekturen und Technologien wie RAG, Vektordatenbanken, AI Agents und Tool Calling
  • Erfahrung mit Infrastructure as Code, beispielsweise Terraform, AWS CDK oder CloudFormation
  • Gute Kenntnisse moderner Software-Engineering- und DevOps-Praktiken, insbesondere Git, CI/CD, automatisiertes Testing und Deployment
  • Erfahrung mit der Entwicklung und Integration von APIs sowie der Anbindung unterschiedlicher Datenquellen und Unternehmenssysteme
  • Verständnis für Security, IAM, Monitoring, Performance, Skalierbarkeit und Kostenoptimierung in Cloud-Umgebungen
  • Idealerweise zusätzliche Erfahrung mit Azure, Container-Technologien oder AI-Frameworks wie LangChain, LangGraph oder vergleichbaren Lösungen
Architekturverständnis und Hands-on-Mentalität: Du kannst fachliche Anforderungen in technische Architekturen übersetzen und bist gleichzeitig in der Lage, diese selbst umzusetzen. Du denkst in Gesamtlösungen, verstehst technische Abhängigkeiten und legst Wert auf wartbare, sichere und produktionsfähige Software.

Intrinsisches Interesse an AI-Innovationen: Du verfolgst die Entwicklungen rund um Generative AI und Agentic AI aktiv, probierst neue Technologien aus und kannst einschätzen, welche Ansätze in realen Kundenprojekten einen Mehrwert bieten.

Stakeholderorientiertes Denken bringt uns weiter: Du arbeitest gerne mit Kunden, Fachbereichen und technischen Ansprechpartnern zusammen. Du kannst Anforderungen strukturiert aufnehmen, unterschiedliche Perspektiven berücksichtigen und komplexe technische Sachverhalte verständlich vermitteln.

Support the Making-of-a-Star: Du unterstützt andere Woodmarker aktiv beim Aufbau von AI- und Cloud-Kompetenzen und teilst deine Erfahrungen und dein Wissen im Team.

Fließende Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse: Du bewegst dich sicher in deutschsprachigen Projekten und kannst technische Dokumentation sowie Architekturkonzepte auch auf Englisch verständlich darstellen.

jobs.description:
Role Title: Research Evaluation Specialist (PhD or Masters / Researcher)

Role Type: Contractor (~15 hs a week)

Location: Remote, worldwide

micro1 is engaging Research Evaluation Specialists (PhD or Masters / Researcher) to contribute expert insight in developing rigorous test material for advanced AI model evaluation as part of a customer's project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. Prior experience in AI is required while your domain knowledge brings high value.

Scope of Work

  1. Create original, high-difficulty question-and-answer pairs at the cutting edge of your discipline to rigorously assess AI model capabilities.
  2. Source, verify, and thoroughly document answers using primary sources and authoritative references, including clear citations and reasoning.
  3. Design questions demanding advanced reasoning, methodological nuance, or synthesis across multiple sources, ensuring resistance to oversimplified or shortcut solutions.
  4. Test questions against AI systems, identify items that are not sufficiently challenging, and iteratively increase complexity while maintaining accuracy.
  5. Write each question and answer with high precision and clarity, eliminating ambiguity and supporting defensible responses.
  6. Integrate reviewer feedback and consistently uphold all project guidelines and quality standards throughout your deliverables.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Masters or PhD completed, active candidacy, or equivalent research experience as a specialist, researcher, assistant professor or professor in your domain.
  2. Demonstrated track record of scholarly research, in-depth subject matter expertise, and familiarity with primary literature.
  3. Exceptional analytical thinking, close attention to detail, and strong written communication skills in English.
  4. Experience sourcing and triangulating information from authoritative references.
  5. Proven self-direction and reliability in delivering expert-level work independently within remote engagements.
  6. Skill in composing challenging, original, and methodologically sound questions.
  7. Prior experience in AI training, data labeling, or model evaluation is required.

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply. Experts must submit a minimum of tasks per week.

Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

This is a rare opportunity to be a key technical voice on Aura's AI Intelligence Platform, which unifies all of Aura's data and bridges the gap between AI agents and that data, with security and privacy as its foundational pillars. This platform is how we turn everything Aura knows about digital threats into timely, personalized insights that protect our customers and their families from harm, whether that's surfacing the one alert that actually matters, helping a parent understand a change in their child's online behavior, or spotting a scam before it lands.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll take on hard technical problems and own them end to end, building the infrastructure that lets AI operate over deeply sensitive information without compromising the security and privacy our customers trust us to hold. You'll work primarily in Python and TypeScript on AWS, on systems that serve millions of Aura customers.

This is a deeply technical, hands-on role. You'll take ownership of complex initiatives from architecture through production, and contribute to the technical direction a growing team of engineers builds on. We're looking for more than a strong coder: someone who brings order to ambiguous problems, sets a high standard for security and privacy engineering, and influences across teams through technical leadership.

Day to Day:

  • Design, document, and drive the architecture for key platform components, ensuring scalability, reliability, security, and alignment with business goals.
  • Own complex initiatives from design and architecture through development, deployment, and iteration, navigating ambiguous product goals and translating them into clear, scalable technical requirements.
  • Build the foundation that unifies Aura's data into a trusted, high-quality source for generating intelligence.
  • Architect how AI agents access and reason over sensitive data, designing for least-privilege access, strong isolation, and enforceable privacy guarantees so intelligence can be generated without ever crossing a data-safety boundary.
  • Build the systems that turn that intelligence into personalized insights and actions that keep our customers and their families safe.
  • Make and defend high-leverage technology choices across the stack, balancing scalability, cost, and operational simplicity.

  • Experience with large-scale data platforms and data-intensive systems.

Job Title: Senior Health Data Analyst - Compass

Job Location: Boston, MA

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.

The Role

As the Senior Health Data Analyst on the Compass Patient Team for Veeva Compass, you’ll focus on the health data in our Compass Patient data product.

Veeva Compass is our suite of data products, with Compass Patient including prescription and medical claims record-level data to support more broad de-identified patient analytics for commercial use cases, like patient journey, market landscape, provider engagement, and more.

You’ll own health data investigations and improvements as part of our Product team. You’ll focus on three key areas:

    1. Data Support - investigate internal and external questions and requests to understand data trends and behavior within customer-defined cohorts and across the network.
    2. Data Quality - Define and track quality metrics in your target domain in dashboards, identify improvement opportunities, and work cross-functionally to document and share learnings.
    3. Data Network Improvements - Collaboratively launch new features to continue to enhance our data in your target expertise area. You’ll focus on investigating, defining and testing productizable improvements that work at scale across billions of records.

This is a great opportunity for someone who is passionate about data and excited about working alongside Product Managers, Customer Success Managers, Engineers, and QA to implement improvements to continue to enrich our data and drive product excellence.

What You’ll Do

    • Own the investigation and resolution of data observations and data questions driven by internal and external stakeholders
    • Understand our product pipeline and impact to data to identify improvements
    • Build standard templates and practices to streamline data quality in your target domains
    • Own key analytics projects in the data and feature roadmaps
    • Design new data analytics and data quality features & capabilities, including features such as match, merge, dedupe logic, value enrichment and reference mappings
    • Establish quality metrics and build dashboards to drive continuous improvement of our data products for key areas such as merging, payer data, lab, prescribers, etc.

Requirements

    • 4+ years of experience analyzing prescription data and medical claims data
    • Advanced SQL skills; able to query and manipulate relational databases
    • Knowledge of Industry Standard billing codes such as ICD, CPT/HCPCS, NDC
    • Experience documenting and presenting analytics results with stakeholders
    • Experience defining KPIs and building dashboards to measure success

Nice to Have

    • Experience in Python
    • Experience with the BI tool Sigma
    • Experience in commercial life science use cases
    • Experience in enterprise products

Interviewing with Veeva

We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.

    • Follow the application process and submit your resume.
    • Within 3 days, you will receive a link to a personality assessment administered by a third party.
    • Once you complete the assessment, our team will review your full application package and follow up via email with our decision.
    • If moving to the interview stage, the process is as follows:
        1. A conversation with the hiring manager
        2. A practical case exercise
        3. A final conversation with our group's Senior Leader.
    • Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision.

Perks & Benefits

    • Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance
    • Flexible PTO and company paid holidays
    • Retirement programs
    • 1% charitable giving program

Compensation

    • Base pay: $80,000 - $125,000
    • The salary range listed here has been provided to comply with local regulations and represents a potential base salary range for this role. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range above or below, depending on experience and location. We look at compensation for each individual and base our offer on your unique qualifications, experience, and expected contributions. This position may also be eligible for other types of compensation in addition to base salary, such as variable bonus and/or stock bonus.
Veeva’s headquarters is located in the San Francisco Bay Area with offices in more than 15 countries around the world.

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Security Assurance to join our GRC engineering team. We are building a security system that’s automated at scale, rigorously data-driven, and built from the ground up with defense-in-depth and self-healing in mind. We support a highly autonomous, remote-first, cloud-native organization. We are a technical team that can build any tool we need, while knowing when to buy to improve velocity.

We are a 100% remote company. We believe in high-velocity but sustainable expectations and timeframes, giving people the room to do great work.

The Opportunity:

You will work to build out our security observability, compliance, and control management systems and tools. You will develop services and tools to proactively defend our systems, provide visibility to our security state, and give engineers and stakeholders guardrails and paved roads to behave securely. You will collaborate across your team, the security department, and wider Grafana to write and deploy security policies across all of our SDLC, applications, and infrastructure.

This is a very technical, hands-on keyboard software engineering, so development experience is critical. You will ideally have some experience building, implementing and improving the maturity of security programs in Cloud-based SaaS organizations. Knowledge of security standards and frameworks (ISO, FedRAMP, PCI-DSS, GDPR, etc) is useful, but the disposition to quickly learn new things is more important than rote knowledge. You will work alongside other security engineers, full-stack developers, and customer-facing teams. Experience guiding and negotiating with peers, stakeholders, customers, and auditors is a plus.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Be a technical contributor on our GRC team covering a range of areas, including certifications, application, build, cloud, and supply chain security, and internal security tooling development
  • Develop, implement, and maintain highly automated security assurance programs to ensure compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements (e.g., ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, NIST, PCI-DSS, TISAX, whatever else our customers eventually throw at us)
  • Develop systems, automations, and methods of security observability to push the GRC engineering organization beyond just meeting certification requirements
  • Deploy security and compliance checks in an employee-enabling way (guardrails and paved roads) in their daily workflows and build pipelines
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate security controls into the software development lifecycle and operational processes.
  • Respond to customer security issues, security alerts, and potential incidents

What Makes You a Great Fit:

  • Experience developing in a production environment with at least one programming language. We primarily use Go, TypeScript, and Python but most languages translate well. You will take a code screen and be expected to discuss programming principles such as algorithms, data structures, and optimization
  • Knowledge of using and securing containerized, cloud-native applications, ideally with Kubernetes. Experience with multiple cloud providers is a strong plus
  • Experience in automating security and compliance processes using tools, scripts, and frameworks while enabling developer and employee workflows
  • Strong interpersonal skills, as this position will require communication with peers, stakeholders, auditors, and customers
  • Understanding of industry-recognized security frameworks, standards, and certifications, such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, NIST, or GDPR, and how to apply them without added operational burden. You can gain this by reading the standards documents and audit guidance
  • A degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or related field (or equivalent experience)

Bonus Points For:

  • Working knowledge of Grafana Labs OSS projects and products. Experience in using observability tooling to solve security problems.
  • Experience working with OSS communities
  • Experience in using technical automations to prove infrastructure compliance
  • Experience securing large-scale distributed systems running in public clouds

In Ireland, the base compensation range for this role is €82,988 - €99,586. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.

  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

jobs.description:
Harbor is seeking a HR Workday Transformation Consultant to advise US clients on HR transformation and Workday, helping them plan, select and deliver change that lasts. Our HR and Payroll Transformation practice is growing quickly in the US, and this role is central to that growth. We advise organizations on how to modernize their HR and payroll functions, from the early business case through to system selection, implementation oversight and post go live support. Much of our work is with professional services firms, particularly large law firms, where we have built a strong reputation for independent, practical advice on Workday.

Our US client base has grown rapidly over the past two years. We now need an experienced consultant on the ground who can lead client conversations, shape engagements and help us win new work. This is a remote position that can be worked from anywhere in the US, with preference given to those candidates located in the Eastern Time Zone near a major metropolitan area.

Responsibilities:

The role splits broadly into five areas, with the balance shifting depending on the client work in hand.

HR Transformation Advisory

  • Lead discovery and current state reviews of HR, payroll and people processes, and set out clear, costed options for change.
  • Build business cases for HR technology investment, including benefits, costs, risks and timelines.
  • Design target operating models for HR and HRIS teams, covering roles, governance, service delivery and support.
  • Advise senior stakeholders, including CHROs, COOs and CFOs, on transformation strategy and priorities.

Workday Advisory and System Selection

  • Run HCM system selection exercises, including Workday against Oracle, SAP SuccessFactors and other platforms.
  • Manage systems integrator (SI) procurement: write RFPs, set scoring criteria, run supplier demonstrations and lead evaluation.
  • Review SI proposals, statements of work and commercial terms, and help clients negotiate a fair deal.
  • Act as the client's independent adviser during implementation, providing quality assurance, design review and challenge to the SI.

Delivery

  • Plan and manage engagements to time, budget and quality, with clear reporting to clients and internal leadership.
  • Support workstreams such as testing, data migration, change management, training and job architecture.
  • Produce high quality client deliverables, including reports, presentations, evaluation packs and operating model designs.

Workday Training for HR Teams

  • Assess training needs across HR, payroll and people operations teams, and design a training plan that fits each role.
  • Deliver Workday training to HR teams, both in person and online, covering core HCM processes, reporting and day to day administration.
  • Create clear training materials, including user guides, quick reference cards, exercises and recorded walkthroughs.
  • Prepare HR teams to support themselves after go live, including train the trainer sessions and handover to internal Workday support teams.
  • Provide refresher and update training as Workday releases new features twice a year.

Business Development and Practice Growth

  • Build and maintain relationships with HR, finance and operations leaders across the US market.
  • Identify new opportunities within existing clients and help shape proposals and pricing.
  • Contribute to thought leadership, events and the development of our methods and tools.
  • Coach and support more junior consultants.

Skills and Experience:

The right person will have at least eight years in HR transformation, with a strong track record on Workday programs.

Essential

  • At least eight years' experience in HR transformation, HR technology or HR operations, ideally with some of that time in consulting.
  • Hands on involvement in at least two full Workday HCM implementations, either as a client lead, program manager or advisory partner.
  • Sound knowledge of Workday HCM and how it fits with payroll, finance and other connected systems.
  • Experience of running or supporting HCM system selection and SI procurement.
  • Proven experience designing and delivering Workday training to HR teams, with the confidence to run sessions for groups at all levels.
  • Good understanding of US HR and payroll practice, including multi state payroll and benefits administration.
  • Confidence working with senior stakeholders and presenting to leadership teams.
  • Excellent written skills, with the ability to produce clear, well-structured client reports.

Desirable

  • Experience in professional services firms, especially law firms, and an understanding of how partner and fee earner roles differ from standard employee models.
  • Workday certification in HCM, Payroll, Compensation or Recruiting.
  • Knowledge of Workday Payroll or third-party payroll providers such as ADP.
  • Experience of global or cross border programs, including work with UK or European teams.
  • A background in business development within a consulting firm.

Other Qualities

We want someone clients trust to tell them the truth, and colleagues enjoy working with.

  • Independent and confident enough to challenge suppliers and clients when needed.
  • Practical and focused on outcomes rather than theory.
  • Comfortable working on your own in a growing market, while staying closely connected to a team across the US and UK.
  • Curious, organized and able to manage several engagements at once.
  • Commercially aware, with a genuine interest in helping the practice grow.

About Us:

Harbor is the preeminent provider of expert services across strategy, legal technology, operations, and intelligence. Our globally integrated team of 900+ strategists, technologists, and specialists navigate alongside our clients – leading law firms, corporations, and their law departments – to provide essential resources and invaluable insights. Anchored in a rich heritage of deep knowledge, steadfast relationships, and mutual respect, our unwavering dedication lies in shaping the future of the legal industry and fostering enduring partnerships within our community and ecosystem.

Vice President of Growth

Location: Remote (U.S.)
Employment type: Full-time
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

About the role

SimpliFed is looking for a Vice President of Growth to build a predictable, capital-efficient growth engine around our best-in-class baby feeding and lactation care.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will personally develop executive relationships, negotiate and close partnerships, and turn those agreements into referrals, completed care, and sustainable revenue. You will own the growth strategy and the execution that makes it work.

Partnerships will remain our primary focus in 2027. You will expand that foundation, build relationships with larger consumer-facing organizations that complement our offering, and strengthen SimpliFed’s own consumer presence through brand positioning, organic discovery, earned media, and social engagement. You will also pursue selective OB opportunities that preserve our curated patient experience and meet our financial and operational requirements.

We are looking for someone who can show how their work produced measurable growth—and who understands that our clinical model, patient trust, and accountability for outcomes are central to our commercial value.

What you’ll own

  • Partnership growth. Expand existing accounts and secure new partners. Build joint activation plans, strengthen referral workflows, and create predictable volume from partners that already reach families at scale.
  • Strategic consumer partnerships. Identify and close relationships with complementary maternal health, mom and baby, and consumer health organizations. Use their established audiences, trusted brands, and marketing reach to connect more families to SimpliFed.
  • Partner value and economics. Build business cases that demonstrate how SimpliFed improves a partner’s offering, engagement, and commercial performance. Prioritize opportunities based on referral potential, economics, implementation requirements, and strategic fit.
  • Partnership execution. Own prospecting, negotiation, launch coordination, performance reviews, renewals, and expansion. Work with internal teams to ensure commercial commitments can be delivered and partners produce results after signing.
  • Consumer channel foundation. Sharpen positioning; lead search engine optimization and answer engine optimization (SEO/AEO); develop earned media and placements on established mom and baby platforms; and reinvigorate social media to build credibility and organic acquisition.
  • Selective OB expansion. Grow existing relationships and activate partners with established commercial teams. Evaluate RFPs and provider or professional services agreements against economics, operational fit, and preservation of SimpliFed’s care pathway. Keep this channel focused without building a broad field sales team.
  • Growth planning and reporting. Own channel priorities, budgets, pipeline, forecasts, and performance reporting. Use demonstrated partnership economics to guide additional DTC investment.
  • Team leadership. Lead a focused team and external specialists or agencies. Set clear expectations, remove barriers, and add resources where results support the investment.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: You have assessed the pipeline, existing partner performance, and patient acquisition journey; established a growth baseline; and built a prioritized plan with owners, milestones, channel economics, and forecasts.
  • First six months: Priority partners have clear activation and expansion plans, new opportunities are progressing toward launch, and the brand, SEO/AEO, earned media, and social strategy is being executed with measurable results.

jobs.excerpt: Remote, U. S. -based · $90,000 OTE ($60,000 base + $30,000 variable) · Launch your sales career Most sales calls sell software.
jobs.description:
Remote, U.S.-based · $90,000 OTE ($60,000 base + $30,000 variable) · Launch your sales career

Most sales calls sell software. Yours will help protect students. The Securly safetyOS™ keeps 20M+ students safe across 20,000+ schools and is credited with helping save 2,400+ student lives, and every district we reach starts with a conversation a BDR opened. If you love the phone, thrive on activity, and want work that matters, this is the role.

Why you'll love this role

  • Real impact: you'll connect schools with the platform that keeps their students safe online, in class, and in the halls
  • A real ramp: structured onboarding and weekly coaching, built for experienced SDRs and career-changers alike
  • Room to grow: we promote from within, and many of our Sales, Customer Success, and GTM leaders started as BDRs
  • Strong pay and benefits: $90,000 OTE, top-tier health coverage, unlimited PTO, and a $1,000 learning stipend
  • Fully remote: work from anywhere in the U.S. with a team that's 82% engaged

The role

You'll own the top of our sales funnel: finding, qualifying, and starting conversations with school districts through cold calls, email, and LinkedIn. You'll introduce district leaders to the Securly safetyOS™, the gold standard for K-12 digital safety and critical IT infrastructure, and hand qualified opportunities to our Account Executives.

You'll report to the Director of Business Development and work closely with Account Executives, Marketing, and RevOps.

What you'll do:

  • Reach out: run high-volume, multi-touch outreach by phone, email, and LinkedIn to K-12 decision-makers
  • Qualify: assess inbound and outbound leads for interest, urgency, and fit
  • Tell the story: share outcomes, customer stories, and market data that show why safetyOS matters
  • Handle objections: listen first and tailor each conversation to what the district cares about
  • Keep it clean: track your work in Salesforce and Outreach.io, using GovSpend and AI Gems for research
  • Hand off well: pass qualified meetings to Sales smoothly, in partnership with Marketing and RevOps
  • Keep improving: use coaching, data, and your peers to get sharper every week

What success looks like

You'll get a structured ramp with coaching at every stage. The milestones below show what the work typically looks like as you build up.

First 30 days

  • Learn the Securly safetyOS™, who we sell to, and how we talk about it, with hands-on coaching
  • Start daily outreach: typically 50–100 calls and 50–200 emails
  • Research your territory and add new prospects to Salesforce every week

Days 60–90

  • Hold 10–25+ meaningful conversations a week with K-12 decision-makers, such as Directors of Technology, IT leaders, superintendents, and district and school administrators
  • Book qualified meetings consistently each month as your pipeline builds
  • Create 8–15+ new sales opportunities a month

By the 6-month mark

  • Run and sharpen outbound prospecting across phone, email, and LinkedIn
  • Use coaching, peer feedback, and your own metrics to keep improving

12 months

  • Consistently meet or exceed your pipeline ($) and quota goals
  • Share what works and help onboard new BDRs
  • Start mapping your next step toward AE or another role in Sales, Customer Success, or adjacent teams

Milestones are typical examples, not fixed requirements. Specific goals are set by your manager and may change based on territory, season, and business needs.

Who we're looking for

Great backgrounds for this role include:

  • Early-career sales: you've worked as an SDR/BDR or in another high-activity outbound role and want to grow in K-12 EdTech. SaaS or EdTech experience is preferred.
  • K-12 educators moving into sales: you're a teacher or school staff member who wants to learn sales and has done sales or sales-like work, ideally with high-volume phone outreach.

Whatever your background, you'll bring:

  • Comfort with high-volume phone calls and outreach, and the drive to keep going after a no
  • Active listening and the ability to ask good questions to engage and qualify prospects
  • The organization to manage a daily cadence and keep clean records (Salesforce and Outreach.io experience is a plus)
  • Curiosity to research prospects and personalize your outreach
  • K-12 education and/or EdTech experience, strongly preferred

What sets you apart:

  • Communication: clear, confident, and adaptive, both verbal and written
  • Growth mindset: you're coachable and treat every call as a chance to get better
  • Prioritization: strong time management and focus on what moves pipeline
  • Rapport: the ability to build trust with IT leaders and K-12 educators
  • AI fluency: comfort using AI tools to research prospects and personalize outreach
  • Mission: a passion for student safety and wellness

Don't check every box? Apply anyway. If you have the drive and the core skills, we want to hear from you.

A realistic look at the job

This is a high-volume, phone-first role. Most days are a steady rhythm of calls, emails, and LinkedIn touches, and many of those won't connect or will end in a no. The reps who thrive here treat that as part of the game, track their numbers, and use coaching to get a little sharper every week. When it clicks, you're booking meetings with district leaders who make decisions about keeping students safe.

This role is fully remote and U.S.-based, No Travel, not offering Visa sponsorship

Where this role leads

We promote from within, and many of our Sales, Customer Success, and GTM leaders started as BDRs. From here, the typical path is Account Executive, with options in Customer Success and other adjacent teams.

Compensation and benefits

Total compensation: $60,000 base + $30,000 variable = $90,000 OTE

  • Top-tier medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Unlimited PTO plus a paid year-end shutdown
  • 12 weeks of paid parental leave
  • Free 24/7 confidential mental health counseling and wellness tools
  • $1,000 annual learning stipend
  • Structured onboarding and ongoing coaching

About Securly

Securly is the market leader in AI-powered student safety and wellness, trusted by 20M+ students across 20,000+ schools. We launched the first cloud-based K-12 web filter in 2013. Today, we've grown into the Securly safetyOS™: the gold standard for global K-12 digital safety and critical IT infrastructure.

safetyOS is one platform for every part of student safety: content filtering, AI governance, 24/7 student wellness monitoring with human-verified alerts, classroom management, digital hall passes, family engagement, and district-wide insights.

The safetyOS™ impact is scaled and trusted:

  • 20% of US K-12 internet traffic is filtered by Securly Filter
  • 1B online activities scanned, generating 50,000 alerts weekly
  • 2M digital hall passes created and managed daily
  • 85K teachers managing 800,000 class sessions weekly

The Securly safetyOS™ is credited with helping save 2,400+ student lives. TIME named us one of America's Top EdTech Companies 2026, and we're a GSV 150 honoree and an EdTech Top 40 “Most Used Product.”

Our people-first culture shows in the numbers (Source: Securly Qualtrics Employee Survey; WSA Global Benchmark):

  • 82% employee engagement, vs. a 73% global benchmark
  • 94% of employees are proud to work here
  • 91% rate manager effectiveness above benchmark

How to apply

Applications close November 3, 2026. We review applications on a rolling basis, so apply early.

Securly is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to a diverse, inclusive workplace. If you need an accommodation during the hiring process, email .

jobs.excerpt: About the Job:LaunchDarkly is looking for a Director, People Programs, Systems & Analytics to establish operational objectives, roadmaps, work plans, and operating rhythms for People programs, systems, analytics, and AI, translating the People Operations strategy and LaunchDarkly’s priorities into executable plans.
jobs.description:
About the Job:

LaunchDarkly is looking for a Director, People Programs, Systems & Analytics to establish operational objectives, roadmaps, work plans, and operating rhythms for People programs, systems, analytics, and AI, translating the People Operations strategy and LaunchDarkly’s priorities into executable plans.

Your team will develop technical and AI-assisted capabilities while turning workforce data into analytics and insights that allow the business to make informed decisions. This role reports to the Senior Director, People Operations.

In this role you will lead a small team and establish the framework for responsible AI use regarding People data. You will partner with Legal, Security, and IT, and recommend solutions that improve reporting, employee support, and efficiency.

Responsibilities:

  • Design the vision, strategy, roadmap, governance, and operating rhythms for all People programs, systems, analytics and AI, in alignment with LaunchDarkly’s business and People priorities. Manage the orchestration and successful completion of organization wide deliverables including OKRs, annual deliverables, and key projects, acting as a visible leader and facilitator within the People organization.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a small, high-performing team, creating clarity, strong partnerships, and a culture of thoughtful execution and continuous improvement.
  • In partnership with the Director, People Operations, ensure that programs and operating processes across the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, employee data, documentation, compliance-related workflows, employee support, and international operations can be optimally managed through our HR tech stack with measurable, decision-informing analytics
  • Design and evolve the People technology ecosystem, ensuring systems are integrated, scalable, secure, fit for purpose, and aligned to the employee and business experience.
  • Establish standards for People data quality, definitions, governance, access, documentation, and stewardship, and build trusted reporting and self-service insights for People partners and business teams.
  • Design an analytics strategy that translates workforce data into executive-ready narratives and practical recommendations across headcount, attrition, hiring, organizational health, employee experience, and workforce planning.
  • Define a responsible AI strategy for the People function, including use-case prioritization, governance, human oversight, and adoption of solutions that improve reporting, decision-making, employee support, and operational efficiency.
  • Partner with the Senior Director, People Operations, functional partners, and subject-matter experts to translate capability gaps into scalable learning experiences, then measure participation, effectiveness, behavior change, business impact, and equity of access.
  • Lead change management for new systems, programs, policies, and processes, including communications, training, stakeholder readiness, adoption, and post-launch improvement.
  • Manage vendors, dependencies, and tradeoffs, bringing structure to ambiguity and maintaining a clear view of value, risk, and long-term scalability.

Qualifications:

  • 15+ years of experience in People Operations, including 5 years leadership across People Programs, People Systems, People Analytics, or a similarly complex function. Experience should include the selection and optimization of HRIS and Talent systems at small and medium- to large-sized companies.
  • A track record of organization-wide project and program management, designing operating models, building roadmaps, and delivering cross-functional programs at scale.
  • Implementation and development of comprehensive data analytics, reporting, and dashboarding tools for Human Resources and Talent organizations with knowledge and experience in AI-enablement for those functions.
  • Experience managing and developing a team and building strong cross-functional partnerships.
  • Experience designing, managing, or improving integrations across HR systems and connected People tools to support reliable data flows and scalable operations.
  • Strong understanding of how People systems, processes, data, and employee programs fit together. Experience improving HR technology, data quality, reporting, analytics, automation, or self-service decision support.
  • Practical experience evaluating or advancing AI use cases, with sound judgment around sensitive employee data, privacy, governance, accuracy, and human oversight.
  • Excellent written communication, prioritization, program management, and change leadership skills.

About You:

  • You are a strategic, systems-oriented People leader who connects technology, data, programs, and human experience.
  • You can set organization-wide direction at the program level while engaging deeply enough to understand implementation details and remove barriers.
  • You are ambitious about innovation, pragmatic about execution, and thoughtful about risk and employee trust.
  • You are curious about People analytics and AI and disciplined about where they should and should not be applied.
  • You are collaborative, grounded, proactive, and committed to building scalable, equitable experiences for employees and managers.

What Success Looks Like:

  • The People team has a clear, prioritized roadmap across programs, systems, analytics and AI.
  • The People team has stronger governance, clearer processes, more reliable data, and fewer manual or fragmented workflows.
  • People partners and business teams have trusted, actionable insights for workforce planning and People decisions, with responsible AI use cases improving efficiency and decision support.
  • The team is engaged, growing, and recognized as a strategic partner that delivers meaningful outcomes across the company.

Pay:

Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level M4:

  • Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $152,900 - 210,210**
  • Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $137,600 - $189,200**
  • Zone 3: All other US locations - $129,900 - $178,640**
  • All Zones inclusive of 15% Bonus Target

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

*Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.
**Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary.

About LaunchDarkly:

Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations.

The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

  • Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages
  • Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts
  • Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize
  • Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types
  • Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability

At LaunchDarkly, we believe in the power of teams. We're building a team that is humble, open, collaborative, respectful and kind. jobs.title: Technical Product Owner, AI-Directed Development
jobs.excerpt: Why CBT Nuggets is a great place to work:Work from anywhere.
jobs.description:
Why CBT Nuggets is a great place to work:

Work from anywhere. While we have an office in Eugene, Oregon, the majority of our team works remotely throughout the United States.
We take work-life balance seriously. You’ll work hard at CBT Nuggets, but you’ll also have plenty of time to relax and recharge. We recognize the importance of spending time with your family and friends — and having time for your hobbies and passions.
Enjoy creative freedom. Got ideas that could benefit our learners and organization? We embrace innovation. We are always open to new ideas — and welcome them from everyone on our team.
Get involved in great causes. NuggetLove, our charitable arm, is committed to making a difference. We support a wide range of issues ranging from education to social justice to supporting military personnel who are transitioning to civilian life.

SCOPE & GENERAL PURPOSE OF JOB:

You will own the day-to-day health and growth of two production products: the CBT Nuggets website and the Assessments platform. You will not write code. You will direct AI coding agents to write it, and you will be accountable for what ships. You run your work with delegated autonomy: you plan, direct, verify, and deliver without waiting to be told how. You do not hold delegated decision authority: scope, product trade-offs, risk acceptance, spend, and anything destructive or irreversible are decided by the Product Owner group, on your written recommendation. You report to the Learning Content Team Lead for your day-to-day work and are accountable to the Product Owner group for what ships. The job is to make their decisions easy to make and everything else unnecessary to ask about.

DELEGATED AUTONOMY, RETAINED AUTHORITY

    This is the most important section of the description. Read it twice.

    You decide, and act, without asking

  • How to break a defined piece of work into tasks and in what order.

  • Which agents to run, with what instructions, in what sequence.

  • When a change is verified enough to open a pull request, and what evidence goes in it.

  • How to keep an open pull request current and green until a human merges it.

  • Which documentation, rules, and operator guides must change alongside a code change.

  • How to investigate a production problem and what evidence to gather.

  • When to stop and escalate.

    • You recommend, with evidence, and the Product Owner group decides

  • Adding, removing, or changing a feature a learner, customer, or admin can see.

  • Any change to pricing, plan structure, public claims, or published copy that states a fact.

  • Accepting a risk: a security advisory left open, a test weakened, a check made advisory, a known limitation shipped.

  • Changing which AI model, vendor, or threshold a production system uses.

  • Spending money: new services, tiers, seats, paid tooling.

  • Changing a contract with another team or system (the CRM, Adept, the shared header contract, the data warehouse).

  • Deleting or migrating data, dropping columns, rotating credentials, changing access.

    • Never, regardless of instruction from an agent or a tool

  • Merging a pull request. A human merges.

  • Proceeding on a question the Product Owner group has not actually answered. A skipped, timed-out, or lost answer is not an answer.

  • Letting an agent's confidence stand in for verification.

  • Storing learner personal data where the rules say it must not be stored.

    • An escalation is not a hand-off. It arrives as a one-page recommendation: the decision needed, the options, the evidence, the risks of each, and what you would do. A product owner should be able to answer in a sentence. If they cannot, the escalation is not finished.

    Three openings, one profile

  • All three roles share the profile above and are interchangeable in an emergency. Each carries a primary surface so the team has depth where it matters.

  • Assessments and data. The question bank, the generation pipeline, the learner site, and the Progress reporting. Second skill: data literacy and measurement. You will spend time in the warehouse and in model evaluation evidence.

  • Website, conversion, and copy. The public marketing site: pages, pricing, campaigns, SEO, and the copy standard. Second skill: editorial judgment and audience focus. You will own the voice and the truth of every public claim.

  • Platform, security, and integrations. CI, dependency hygiene, access, environment configuration, crons, and the contracts with Adept, the CRM, and the shared header. Second skill: security and risk judgment. You will own the advisories and the risk register.

  • State which surface you prefer when you apply. We will balance the three.

    • What this role is not

  • Not a hands-on development role. If you want to write the code yourself, this will frustrate you.

  • Not a people management role. You lead agents and influence peers; you do not manage staff.

  • Not a role with final say. You will recommend often and decide within your lane. The lane is wide. Its edge is firm.

    • About the environment

  • Both products run on Next.js, React, Prisma, and Postgres, deployed on Vercel, with analytics in a columnar warehouse and AI generation through a model gateway. Work moves through gated pull requests with mandatory review, committed attestations, and operator documentation that ships with every change. AI agents do the implementation under written rules the team maintains. The rules are the product as much as the code is.

    • MEASURES OF SUCCESS:

  • First 30 days. You have shipped changes through the full gated workflow on both products. You have read the operating rules and can explain why each exists. You have found and corrected at least one stale claim in the documentation.

  • First 90 days. You own a surface. Your pull requests arrive green and stay green. Your escalations are answerable in a sentence. You have written at least one durable rule from a lesson you learned, and retired one that was stale.

  • First year. The Product Owner group can leave your surface for a month and return to find it healthier, better documented, and with a short, well-argued list of decisions waiting. Nothing shipped that they would not have approved. Nothing waited that they would have approved in a sentence.

    • How we will evaluate you:

  • Specification exercise. Given a short product request, write the specification you would hand to an agent. We are reading for precision, missing cases, and whether you identified what needs a decision from the Product Owner group.

  • Review exercise. Given a pull request with an agent-written summary that over-claims, find it, say how you found it, and say what rule would prevent it next time.

  • Escalation exercise. Given a situation with real trade-offs, write the one-page recommendation. We are reading for whether the decision-maker can answer in a sentence.

  • Business conversation. Tell us what you learned about CBT Nuggets from public sources and what you would want to measure first.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

    Learn the CBT Nuggets business: who buys, why, at what price, and what the data says about it. Read the warehouse and the CRM well enough to check a number yourself.

  • Own a backlog for your surface. Turn product intent into precise written specifications an AI agent can execute without guessing.

  • Direct AI coding agents through the full change lifecycle: specification, implementation, review, tests, documentation, pull request, CI, and production verification.

  • Read every diff critically. Find the over-claim in an agent's summary before a reviewer does.

  • Operate the repositories as a professional: branch protection, required checks, rebases, attestations, dependency advisories, environment variables, crons, feature flags, deployments.

  • Keep the operator documentation true. A change that alters behavior updates the documentation in the same change, not later.

  • Turn every lesson into a durable, dated rule that the next agent and the next teammate must follow. Retire rules that have gone stale.

  • Investigate production incidents from logs, metrics, and the database, and write up what happened and what prevents it.

  • Measure before you claim. Date every reading. Record when an earlier reading turned out to be wrong.

  • Reduce friction for other humans. When a decision or a labeling task needs a person, build them a page with buttons and send a link, not a document with instructions.

  • Work in the open with your two teammates: shared rules, shared conventions, no private process.

SKILLS/COMPETENCIES/EDUCATION:

  • Skills/experience required:

  • Five or more years in IT or software, in roles that required understanding how production systems are built, deployed, secured, and operated. Systems administration, network engineering, DevOps, QA engineering, solutions engineering, technical support leadership, and software development all qualify.

  • At least one year directing AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or equivalent) to ship production software, with examples you can walk through: what you asked for, what the agent got wrong, how you caught it, what you changed so it did not happen again.

  • Two or more years of product ownership or technical product management: owning a backlog, writing specifications, making prioritization calls, and being accountable for outcomes rather than tickets.

  • Demonstrated evidence of discipline. You verify claims against the system, not the document. You can describe a time a confident source was wrong and how you found out.

  • Fluency as an operator in GitHub (pull requests, CI, branch protection, merge conflicts, force-with-lease), a hosting platform such as Vercel, and a relational database such as Postgres. You read SQL and diffs critically even though you do not author the code.

  • Clear, plain written English. Short sentences. No hedging that hides a decision. You can write a rule, a specification, and a one-page recommendation that a busy executive can act on.

  • Comfort being accountable for work you did not type, and comfort escalating without ego when a decision is not yours.

  • Independent thinker and self-starter

  • Attention to detail

  • Collaborative and comfortable working on a team

  • Attitude required:

  • Honesty, humility, and integrity

  • Inclusive and respectful

  • Strong work ethic

  • Passion for learning

  • Comfortable with autonomy

  • Eager to add new skills and grow professionally

  • Skills that are preferred, but not required:

  • Experience with Next.js, React, Prisma, Postgres row-level security, OAuth, or a columnar analytics warehouse. You will not write it, but you will read it daily.

  • Experience evaluating AI models for production use: A/B measurement, calibration, cost per output, and knowing when the evidence says do not adopt.

  • Security and privacy judgment: dependency advisories, supply-chain overrides, PII boundaries, risk acceptance with an expiry date.

  • Product marketing or editorial experience, in particular writing to an IT Director or Training Manager audience with every claim checked against the product.

  • Experience in IT training, certification, e-learning, or assessment design.

  • Experience negotiating integration contracts with another engineering team

  • Curiosity

  • Assertiveness

  • A love of IT and/or technology

  • Ability to be proficient with an Apple laptop

  • Proficiency with Gmail, Google Docs, Slack, and internal CBT Nuggets software

CLASSIFICATION/COMPENSATION/BENEFITS:

  • This position is a full-time (40 hours per week) salaried position, exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act

  • Compensation for this role is $100,000 per year

  • Generous employee benefits

CBT NUGGETS MISSION

To continually improve the effectiveness of learning.

CBT NUGGETS BRAND COMPONENTS:

Position: The distinct point of difference our brand holds in the minds of our target audience.
- IT training you can trust.
Personality: The human traits that describe our brand as if it were a person.
-Passionate, empathetic, and accountable.
Promise: The consistent experience we commit to providing at every touchpoint.
- Learner First

Interviewing Tips

What you say doesn’t matter nearly as much as what you do. Prove to us that you have passion, attention to detail, a good work ethic, and are an independent thinker through your preparation for the interview. Imagine yourself as already having the job and focus on telling us how you will help CBT Nuggets accomplish its mission with your help.
Sign up for the free trial and learn about the CBT Nuggets offering. Every teammate at CBT Nuggets has to understand our customer and our product. Prepare as if you’re already on the team.
Don’t be nervous, there’s no reason to be. If you feel nervous, channel that energy into better use.
Smile, and enjoy the process.

Third-Party Solicitation

Headhunters and recruitment agencies may not directly submit applications for this job posting and are expressly prohibited from reaching out directly to any hiring managers or department heads via phone, email, LinkedIn, or other means of communication. All applications must be submitted directly by the job applicant."

jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewAt Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department Overview

Silvus Technologies, a leading provider of advanced MANET and MIMO communications systems, is reshaping mesh network technology for mission-critical applications – on the ground, in the air and at sea. Its battle-proven StreamCaster family of MANET radios and proprietary MN-MIMO waveform provides the vital communications link for defense, law enforcement and public safety agencies around the world, and in the toughest operational environments.

Silvus Technologies is a wholly owned subsidiary of Motorola Solutions, Inc.


Job Description

Would you like to join an incredibly talented group of people, doing very challenging work, with the prime directive of “Keeping Our Heroes Connected”?


THE OPPORTUNITY

Silvus is seeking a highly motivated Technical Product Manager (TPM) (Spectrum Dominance) to drive technical requirements, backlog ownership, market adoption, and revenue growth of our Spectrum Dominance product portfolio. This position will report to the Director of Product Management on the Product team. The successful individual in this role will play a vital role in translating complex defense requirements and highly advanced R&D algorithms into software features, firmware builds, and intuitive operator experiences. This is an execution-focused role that acts as the key technical conduit between our advanced waveform R&D team and our engineering, operations, and go-to-market teams.


The Technical Product Manager will take technical ownership of Silvus' spectrum dominance suite. Their mission is to translate complex mathematical algorithms and signal processing research—specifically in Low Probability of Intercept / Low Probability of Detection (LPI/LPD) and anti-jamming into actionable requirements. By bridging the gap between theoretical R&D and reliable military systems engineering, the Technical Product Manager will ensure Silvus outpaces emerging electronic warfare (EW) threats and delivers robust software-defined spectrum dominance.


This position is located at Silvus Technologies’ Engineering and R&D Office in Irvine, CA, near the vibrant Irvine Spectrum and is on a hybrid schedule, with one day reporting to our West Los Angeles HQ. On-site days are Mondays, Tuesdays, and Wednesdays at our Irvine office and Thursdays at our West Los Angeles HQ. However, this position is eligible for 100% remote work depending on location for candidates based in the US, with a willingness to travel up to 25-50% of the time to support field testing, customer integrations, customer meetings, and Silvus office locations.


The following is a list of at least some of the current essential job functions of the position. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities at any time at its discretion.

ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Product Definition & Technical Execution

  • Requirements Engineering: Translating abstract DoD mission requirements, mathematical signal analysis concepts, and electromagnetic spectrum operations needs into highly structured user stories and technical specifications.
  • Algorithm-to-Feature Translation: Directly partnering with R&D engineering to translate complex, cutting-edge LPI/LPD and anti-jam techniques into a clear feature set with an intuitive operator experience.
  • Product & Waveform Ownership: Owning the end-to-end software and firmware backlog, requirements definition, and user experience for the spectrum dominance features.
  • Technical Waveform Alignment: Partnering with the R&D and software engineering teams to ensure advanced waveforms integrate seamlessly with our MN-MIMO architecture and flagship StreamCaster hardware platforms.

Tactical Lifecycle & Agile Backlog Management

  • Sprint & Backlog Ownership: Conducting highly disciplined sprint planning, backlog grooming, and release cadences via Jira to ensure a predictable and rapid delivery pipeline of spectrum dominance software and firmware updates.
  • Scope & Trade-off Analysis: Conducting technical and schedule analyses of customer and sales feature requests, evaluating engineering development timelines, and establishing strict scope boundaries to balance schedule constraints against field expectations.
  • Closed-Loop Feedback Integration: Systematically capturing operational feedback, field trial results, and operator testing notes to continuously evolve backlog user stories and transform field-tested waveforms into robust commercial software solutions.
  • Post-launch Performance and Adoption: Responsible for product adoption and collaborating with sales to generate interest and revenue growth for the products. Measuring and monitoring product performance, defining continuous software refinement cycles to address user experience debt or newly discovered threat vectors and continuing to capture customer and field feedback for product updates.

Customer Integration & Cross-Functional Alignment

  • Cross-Functional Synergy: Bridging the gap between R&D, software engineering, operations, and the GTM teams to align product execution with broader business strategy, software monetization, licensing, and delivery timelines.
  • Operational Feedback Loop: Translating market intelligence, upcoming DoD program specifications, and competitor threat assessments into strategic backlog priorities to maintain Silvus' market-leading technology edge.
  • Travel Requirements - Ability to travel up to 25% of the time to support field testing, customer integrations or customer meetings.
  • Perform other related duties of which the above are representative.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, RF Engineering, or a highly related technical discipline.
  • Minimum of 5 years of technical product management or systems engineering experience within the defense, aerospace, or wireless communications industries.
  • Strong working knowledge of signal processing, wireless communications, RF systems, software-defined radios (SDRs), digital signal processing (DSP), or mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs).
  • Demonstrated experience translating highly complex mathematical algorithms, scientific concepts, or military use cases into structured, clear, and actionable software requirements and user stories.
  • Proven ability to influence and align cross-functional R&D, engineering, operations, and sales teams without direct authority to meet strict release timelines.
  • Security Clearance: Active U.S. Government SECRET clearance or the ability to obtain one within 15 months of hire.
  • Must be a U.S. Citizen due to clients under U.S. government contracts.
  • All employment is contingent upon the successful clearance of a background check and drug test.

PREFERRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Hands-on experience with Low Probability of Intercept / Low Probability of Detection (LPI/LPD), electronic counter-countermeasures, anti-jamming, or spectrum monitoring solutions.
  • Familiarity with passive RF sensing, spectral analysis, Direction Finding, Angle of Arrival localization, or tactical signal intelligence systems.
  • Understanding of government compliance targets, military environmental standards (MIL-STD), or security certifications (e.g., FIPS 140-3 and CSfC validation architectures).
  • Master’s degree in Engineering, RF Engineering, Computer Science, or an MBA from an accredited institution.
  • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development practices and managing complex backlogs using tools like Jira.

WORKING CONDITIONS AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Office environment.
  • Trade shows.
  • Outdoor environment for demonstrations.
  • Occasional exposure to heat, cold, and allergens while performing tests or demonstrations in the field.
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to do the following:
    • Lift equipment up to 50 lbs. for the set-up of demonstrations and testing.
    • Perform bending and reaching movements to place items on lower and higher shelves.
    • Kneeling or squatting to access lower shelves.
    • Walking/Moving in the labs.
